Really Big Sky is a side scrolling, roguelite twin-stick shmup that I can't compare to any shooter from my memory. Unlike most shmups, it falls less on the inherent skill requirement and more on the trial and error style such as a Contra. It has that bright and colorful style like Geometry Wars and unique gameplay mechanic involving shifting the ship between standard shooting mode and drill mode. The standard mode utilizes laser backdraft - in which your shot becomes larger and more powerful after not shooting for a moment, so it pays not to "always be shooting" like other shmups have taught you (This is probably easier with the Controller as you're always shooting when using the mouse and keyboard until you click). The drill mode disables your shot, but allows you to bore through planets and meteors and use a limited count drill spin (that makes a sound much like Sonic the Hedgehog's spin dash).
Besides what appears to be randomly occuring "smart bomb moves", that is the limit of your ability (besides moving of course). RBS cleverly and annoyingly uses these limited mechanics to anger you and challenge you. Even the experienced shmuper will likely die often due to the curveballs of incoming solid planets, inconveinient laser beams, or deviously placed meteor fields. What makes that worse is that the the art style is a bit much at times and RBS will put salt on the wound by having random events that you have never encountered before such as inverting the color palette or navigation challenge events like from Scoregasm or Satazius. I thought I would eventually get over this, but the artstyle is at times, so flashy that you're likely to get hit by something you couldn't quite see in the chaos. Oh, and the game will occassionally mock you via the announcer or saying your skill level is "N00B". You will probably die often, more likely from planets and events than the bullet hell streams, but that is part of the intent, as it utilizes the modern roguelike trend of allowing you to upgrade your ship after you lose. Shards from killed enemies are used as currency to buy upgrades such as 45, 90 and 180 degree shots, shields to absorb damage, claymores that cause explosions and seem to cancel a few bullets, and much more. Said shards often spray in a fashion that makes it impossible to get them all and can place you in danger. Admittedly, the upgrades are a bit confusing as it isn't always clear when they are activated or being used (why do some upgrades say "co-op" when I can use them in single player?) and I'm not sure why I randomly get a vortex that will duplicate my shot pattern (I think it's another random event like the giant laser attack you can get). Despite it's simplicity, parts of this game are confusing.
The game does have a lot to offer - like most roguelikes, you almost never play the same level though I can't tell if they are either completely procedurally generated, or if there is a pool of randomly selected levels. Even in the different levels, there are a variety of enemy types (like shielders that don't hurt you, but block your shots, or cascading enemies from the top of  the screen, or minibosses that have light bullet hell streams). There are a plenty of modes, including Pacifism that removes your ability to shoot, Retro mode which forces your shots to only go forward and adds an annoying posterization color filter, Arcade which spawns more enemies and events, and Boss rush, which honestly, I found pretty fun, even early in the game (best mode?). The soundtrack is solid and energetic use of electronica, synthwave and to my suprise, some metal in boss rush.

I have so many mixed feelings about this game.
I played the series in order. I first played Saints Row on the ole 360 and couldn't put it down. I stopped supporting consoles before Two was released and had to wait until I could get it on the PC to play it. I had a hell of a time putting that one down too. Then, I played The Third......
Saints Row Two was just so great and had just about everything I could want from a Sequel to the first game.
Saints Row The Third on the other hand, is a rather heavy let down. My feelings towards sequals is that I don't feel like they should take away good content. If it works....keep using it! Add, add, add. That's what Saints Row Two did. Shiny graphics are nice, but should never, ever be enough to warrant the massive removal of content. I will admit that I haven't finished The Third, but I have progressed far enough and played long enough that I feel like I have a good sense of the game. Much of what I loved from 2, was removed.
The story, what little of it there is, pales in comparison to the previous games and is actually rather subpar. Side missions like Hits and Chopshops actually had wonderful little cutscenes in One and Two, and I absolutely loved them. I looked forward to them every time I played. Those have been removed in The Third. Now everything is done via phone calls and texts and normally only has some short dialog, if even that. The diversity of the series has also taken a huge dive. There were tons of cars in One and Two, yet I feel like I just keep seeing the same things in The Third. Locations feel plain and over used. One, and more so Two, had tons of unique locations and actually got you to explore the city and drive around to find all the shops and locations. The Third tries to shove everything into one or two shops and it gets old, FAST.
Characters have been so drastically altered to the point that the majority of returning characters are only recognizable by their names. Shaundi, who in 2, was a short stoner with dreads and not much in a fight, has been turned into a tall, skinny, big breasted girl of action and anger. I'm not against that type of character, but did they really have to remodel an existing character, and a good one at that? Couldn't they just have introduced a new girl? Wouldn't have been such a big deal, since the new Shaundi is pretty much that anyway. They even replaced her voice actress, which is a shame since Shaundi is the only time I have ever enjoyed Eliza Dushku as an actress. I believe Pierce retained his voice actor, but has still been overhauled. Though, not as much as Shaundi. One of the things that made Pierce so enjoyable in 2, was how he could do no right. He was a great character and actually quite helpful at times, but no one really took him seriously and often shrugged off his ideas. He was a good character to pick on. They still make jabs, but he often just comes off as more of a man with a plan. He kinda lost his....I don't know, Pierceness? Gat didn't change too much, but he also didn't get much screen time.
The player character is....interesting. You can tell the voice actors had fun with it, which does make me happy, but my favorite voice from Saints Row 2, was sadly no where to be found. The Black female, voiced by G.K. Bowes, was absent from the game and the closest thing to replacing it was a hispanic voice. Now, don't get me wrong, I actually like the hispanic voice, a lot, actually, but it was weird enough to go from playing a semi silent male in One, to playing a very chatty female in Two. It was my choice, but still took some getting used to. I didn't check the male voices, so I can't judge them, but I found that the female voices came off as kinda....I don't know.....not Gangsta. Then again, the game itself it no longer gansta. I think the acting was good, great even, I'm not going to criticize the quality, but they just aren't the voices/accents I would have chosen. In fact, playing a black female character is almost impossible to enjoy, as the only voices you have to pick from are super white girly girly. Deeper Russian accent. Hispanic accent. And one other one, I think. Zombie, maybe?
The gameplay was fun, but often felt a little too easy. The gang feel of the previous games has been replaced by a rich people Vs rich people setting. They kept a lot of Saints Rows trademark humor, and even upped it quite a lot, but even that wasn't enough to make up for what was lost. The game feels somewhat hollow and souless, and I find it impossible to play the game without reminiscing about One and Two.
The DLC is a slightly different story and actually shined more than all of what I have experienced of the main game. It adds some great missions and actually puts some story into it, even if a lot of it is still just characters talking over gameplay. Some of it makes fun of Pierce, which made me happy. You briefly get super powers, which was just fantastic, but that isn't carried over to the main game and is merely tied to a short mission.
Genki is fun but gets a little repetitive after awhile, but the announcer dialog is some of my favorite in the game.
The absurdity level is through the roof, when compared to the first two games, which I can't really complain about, but without the in depth story and more serious tone to balance it, I think it loses a little something.
The weird thing is that, despite my disappointment with the game and aaaaaalll of my complaints, I still recommend it. It's a good game in itself, and can be a fun romp, but I can't say it's a good sequel and I feel like it really only feels like a bad game when you compare it to it's predecessors. But it is a sequel and thus I personally lack the willpower to NOT judge it as such and to NOT compare it to it's predecessors. It is pretty and it has some great qualities, but I think I'm just too stuck in the past to fully enjoy the game.

EDF is some jolly, campy, arcadey fun. Imagine a cross between Starship Troopers, Mars Attacks (minus the Martians) and Dynasty Warriors, and you might get a rough idea what you're in for.
The game offers almost a hundred missions that will either drown you in giant insects as if they're bullets in a bullet hell shooter, or have you duke it out with a horde of giant robots that can easily stretch across the entire horizon. Not to mention truly gigantic bosses.
In contrast to the earlier game Insect Armageddon on Steam (same series, different developer), EDF 4.1 returns to the typical Japanese insanity of the classic series. Health power-ups and weapons are now again gotten solely through loot, for that little bit of Diablo-style weapon farming.
EDF 4.1 also returns to having much shorter missions, but offering a whole lot more of them. And the hectic action of EDF really works best in short, but intensive bursts.
While Insect Armageddon wasn't the most liked in the franchise, it is nice of the original developers to honor the IA team by adapting the two new classes introduced in that earlier game to the classic-style of EDF, cranking them up to 11 like everything else in the game.
So aside from the versatile Ranger and the flight-capable Wing Diver, we have the support-oriented Air Diver who makes up for his lack of direct-fire weapons with mini-turretsand the ability to call in air strikes and vehicles (mostly tanks and mechs, some of which can get pretty huge, as in Godzilla huge). The Fencer with his power armor on the other hand is essentially a man-sized Armored Core, dual-wielding ridiculously huge guns and able to equip melee weapons with literally earth-shattering results.
Performance-wise, the port is very, very well done. Gameplay is smooth (even smoother than in the much older Insect Armageddon it seems) and can handle a crapton of enemies without a noticable slow-down. I did turn off shadows though, seeing how much enemies you typically face in this game.
Controls are very good and responsive (though I do miss the sprint button from Insect Armageddon). Can't say much about keyboard and mouse controls as I'm more of a controller guy for these types of games.
Long story short: Get this game. EDF! EDF!

I'm not going to tell you what this game isn't or what it could be, I'm just here to let you know what it currently is and what it's like with a party of close IRL friends. You will question your sanity. You will second guess what you know about people. Hell, you may even come to realize your friends could lie themselves out of murder charges (okay, maybe not this one).
Deceit is a game that relies almost entirely on your ability to keep calm and lie your way to the finish line. Nobody is to be trusted, even if the burden of proof seems too good to be true. Think you saw someone drink a blood bag? Is someone looking suspicious hiding in a corner all alone? Are you 110% certain all the infected were dealt with nice and early? My dear readers you could be, and will be, DEAD wrong.
This game throws back to the classic Trouble in Terrorist town, some have even compared it to Secret Hitler or Mafia. Of the 6 people in-game, 2 of them are randomly infected and will do ANYTHING it takes to get the remaining 4 innocents to turn on each other. Whether it be through calculated planning or full on mayhem and confusion, it's all about the mind-games. There is no "winning" strategy, there is no "meta" that everyone follows to win, it's all about how well you can convince other people to listen to you whether infected or not. If congressmen played this game you wouldn't even stand a fraction of a chance.
Between all the items and fool-proof ways to determine who is innocent or infected, there is an equal amount of psychological warfare happening at all times. Take the inspector kit for example, it will tell you with 100% accuracy the nature of the person you are scanning. You might be thinking "hey, I could just scan Bob over here, and tell the group if this dude is infected and we're already 1 step ahead right? RIGHT!?"
Wrong. Bob has a darker plan in mind, he says you are lying out of your♥♥♥♥♥and defaults the blame saying YOU are the infected one. Who's to be trusted in this situation? Do they kill Bob possibly putting down one of the infected? Or do they start to believe you ARE really infected, and they chance to take you out and make their lives easier?
What about if one of the infected persons scans the OTHER infected persons and calls him clean, can you believe with 100% certainty that neither of them are lying? The simple answer is: you can't trust ANYONE without seeing the proof yourself.
At the end of it all, it doesn't matter how skilled you are with a gun or how well you know the maps to be able to loot up faster than anyone. If you just don't have the ability to lie yourself out of trouble, you will not escape/kill your victims. This alone adds a nearly infinite amount of replayability, as no 2 minds think alike and people you "think" are on the same wavelength as you can completely deceive you and eat your face off in a dark room with nobody to hear you screaming.
So I'll ask you now; Do you think you have what it takes your lie your way to the finish line? The answer just might surprise (or eat) you.

Ever since the update in Januari (2017) I can no longer support this game as player, tester and translator, nor give it a good recommendation. The game's initial goal - make a very realistic fishing sim for both casual and hardcore players - has changed into grabbing as much money from the community as possible.
Though I understand that the devs need to make a living, the way they are handling it is flawed imho. Prices were raised - like going from €60 to €100 for the biggest BC pack, and being brought to the community as a 'sale' with 10% off without mentioning the raised prices. Name change used to be free, but it now costs you 160 BC which is €10. Unlimited licenses are no longer purchaseble through common in-game currency. A quick math shows that if you want to have them all, you need to hand over almost €380 worth of BC's. That's not mentioning gear that can only be bought with BC's. And the dlc's that are released in the past couple of months are nothing but reskins of already existing gear with a price range from €15 to as high as €65.
The casual players and newcomers in particular have a very rough time. The game in it's current state no longer helps you progress and learn the game. Instead it forces you to grind for hours on end to cover the license fees, traveling expenses and repair costs so you can just make a break even, even if you stay at the area for days in a row. Mistakes are punished severly: if you forgot to purchase the advanced license and caught a trophy fish you shouldn't have, you'll get a 10K fine.
And then the competitions: one of the few ways to earn BC's while not drawing your wallet. Oh, but hang on, you do need to draw your wallet. Because in most competitions the winner is determined by the amount of fish they have in their keepnet. At lower levels you don't have access to those keepnets, unless you purchase them through DLC, meaning that almost always it's the players that paid for it that end up winning them.
The bugs that are known since the beginning of this game arriving on Steam - 2015 -  are still not being adressed. Lure attraction is just a guess, there is no logic behind them. The indicator is still broken, making it hard for newcomers to see if they're doing their retrievals right. Some fish still don't loose stamina regardless if you fight them for hours on end.
Granted, the game still does look amazing and there is no other fishing game out there yet that can compete with it when it comes to looking very realistic. But all in all this game has moved from a great casual as well as hardcore fishing sim, to a grinding pay-to-win arcade game. Given the devs actions over the past six months and their comments - on occassion even bashing players that refuse to pay - they are not willing to move it in another direction. So safe yourself the frustration and money. This game isn't worth it.

An amazing game recreating the retro 2D platformers. If you love the retro and difficult 2D platformers then get this. The game is funny, challenging, inovative, creative, and overall great. Levels, bosses, upgrades, and gameplay is designed very well. The checkpoint system is creative because you can destroy a checkpoint for some gold or keep it so you don't have to backtrack when you inevitably fall into a bottomless pit. Roaming stages are awesome, but there's only like 4 to 5 of them. The levels are designed well but there are very few of them compaired to retro 2D platformers.
Although for $15 it does lack content (look at reviewer's play time it's around 8-20 hours). Also most of your deaths will come from falling into bottomless pits. No matter how much health upgrades you buy or relics you use, if you fall into a bottomless pit (or touch spikes but you can use a relic to avoid them), you die. This wouldn't be a problem exept sometimes the last checkpoint is far behind or a boss kicks you off. Nothing ruins a boss like an attack that one shot kills you (imo). Although I say it's challenging the penalty for death isn't restarting a level like some retro 2D platformers. You only lose some money and go back to the last checkpoint. Sometimes you might get stuck on certain parts for quite awhile and it can get frustrating, but with infinite lives the worst it gets is frustration.
I do recommend the game, but I personally think I shouldn't have bought it since I've never really enjoyed the retro 2D platformers as much as others. If you want to relive those game then get this. If you have never played those kinds of games and want to experience them then pick this up on sale.
EDIT: With the new expantions bringing in plague knight and spectre knight I can say this game definitly has the content to go with its price. PROS:
-Solid, tight gameplay with great level design and challenging, varied enemies.

-Graphics hold up pretty well for such an old game! Run an enb to remove the color filter and the game looks fantastic.

CONS:
-While the Co-op Partner doesn't get in the way too much. it's resource management left a lot to be desired. Stop picking up handgun ammo when we don't even have one in our inventory, Sheva!
-9 inventory slots, feels clunky to switch in mid-combat. Sheva keeps picking up Handgun ammo using up an extra slot.
-Story is completely forgettable since it takes itself a little to seriously to enjoy it. There's no really dumb Leon S. Kennedy one-liners or midget Spanish Napoleon so give this game a fun side, nor do any characters really feel interesting or fleshed out. But when Chris punches that boulder, all is right with the world.
- Some bosses have either a weird hitbox or vague strategies involved, mostly because it's not conveyed well. Final boss' hitboxes are a little wierd, and the
battle lets you shoot the weak point until it requires a QTE finish, which it doesn't tell you to do. (This is minor.)
-That turret section is boring.
Overall pretty dang solid.

Drifting is the name of the game here and that's precisely what you're gonna get.
Drift around that pole! Sweet!
Now jump over that lake! Awesome!
Get them donuts going on that helipad! Cool!
That's basically it. There's a free-roam mode which consists of several zones with mini-objectives as well as separate events scattered around. Get to the zone, complete objectives, unlock the next one - repeat until you're the drift master.
Events are instances in which you can rack up your personal score and compete with other players via the leaderboards. You have 3 lap drift courses of varying difficulty, driftkhanas, which essentially are closed off arenas in which you race against time to get the highest score possible and you have drift tracks in which you go from point A to point B and get as many points as you can along the way.
The game is short, if you're aiming to 'complete' it. If you're here for the pleasure of drifting though, you can spend hours upon hours perfecting your skills.
The presentation is fantastic with very slick, clean and, most importantly, clear visuals. Music is very catchy and complements the picture in the best possible way.
All in all - if you like stylish visuals, racing and drifting, treat yourself with this little gem.

I am new to this game series, and it was a welcome refreshment. The style is super japanese, and reminds me of those old coin-op games. The sounds, the effects and gameplay is very arcade'ish. Can be a bit frustrating sometimes since skill alone is not enough on the hardest levels, and often you see death coming a mile away but there is nothing you can do about it if you are in the middle of a long reload sequence while you are walking away at the speed of a turtle while hordes of insects is flooding over you. This means you will need to grind a lot to collect enough armor and find the right gun for the job.
The many weapons and multiple choices for characters allows you to deploy a lot of different strategies to win, and although it is first of all an action game, your wits at strategy is what will determine wether you will win or not.
The graphics looks a bit old, but it makes up for it by a great physics engine allowing you to destroy almost anything, including huge buildings. The game gives you a grand feeling of scale and power, and the insects move around in a creepingly realistic way.
If you have a high end computer with a high resolution screen, you wont be able to take advantage of its full power. The graphics will be scaled up from a lower resolution and stretched to fill the screen (seems the highest real resolution is 1080p?). Only text will render in the native resolution. However, it is not a big deal since the textures are pretty low resolution anyway, and the blocky graphics kind of gives it even more that retro coin-op feel. I would appreciate if they added support for a higher resolution and better 21:9 aspect ratio support though.

This game is a joke. Its trying SO HARD to be Resi 4 in just about every way but falls falt on its own face. The characters do not have the charm of Resi 4, the enemies are either extremly forgettable or a repeated character from before, the story is so over the top and crazy that you forget what the hell you are doing, the dialogue is so forced and awkward, the entire game lacks the subtlety of Resi 4/REmake, the co-op mechanics are unbelievably forced, and the entire game is as interesting as a wet newspaper on the road. Why is this co-op? The only "co-op" parts are both players hitting switches together, throwing each other over <blank> to eventually meet up a minute later with nothing major occuring, or "sharing" each other inventory, which remarkibly is worse than Resi 4 (9 boxes, each holds a weapon/armor/ammo. an egg takes up as much space as a shotgun).
Health/ammo is abundant, so the "survival" aspect to this game is thrown out the window. If you have played Resi 4, you will most likely never die, even on the hardest difficulty (except for some boss battles, as their damage feedback is so poor you have no idea if what you are doing hurts them unless the game is directly showing you with a healthbar). Enemies usually appear 10 meters in front of you and/or have a long-♥♥♥ cutscene showing you them and their weak point, completely removing any horror or tension in the air. Everything is so boring and pretictable, it feels like a terrible Hollywood blockbuster and NOT a Resi game. If Capcom wants to make an action game, go ahead! Just DO NOT slap on a Resi label.
If you approach this game as a parody of Resi 4, you will get a lot more enjoyment out of it than assuming its an actual Resi game.

After hiding in the dark from this game (not watching any youtube videos) to gain my own knowledge of this game, I was wondering "Was this overhyped?"
Before I answer it, let's talk about the game. As a completely blind experience, I found learning how to play was actually surprisingly easy, and finding secrets was very fun. Gold was a useful currency, and it didn't feel very 'grindy'. Having death make you lose part of your gold made the game somewhat challenging.
The difficulty curve was quite amazing. I never found it too hard or too easy. I always found I had just enough stuff to scrape through, or I needed to go back and get something else to help along.
The items you gain are somewhat unique, and they all have their own uses. Finding out what they did never was too hard.
The upgrades never made the game amazingly easy, they just made doing things a little different.
The achievements add a lovely layer of replayability... I really have nothing else to say about that...
It's an amazing game, so, to answer the question "Was this overhyped?". OF COURSE NOT! I don't even remember the hype, I just remember people playing this game and loving it. And now, I've played it and loved it.
Why not try it out and see how you feel?

So far I've only spent about 20 minutes playing the game. I haven't tried it with a keyboard/mouse yet because of some warnings I've come across, so I cannot personally recommend a controller over a keyboard and mouse. I love the concept, infact, I love the game! The missions in Free Play are fun to do and fun to look for. The drift tracks and tutorials are setup very nicely. Even the games soundtrack is nice, some chill electro EDM music. All around the game is great.
However... I can't seem to grasp the drifting mechanic. One moment I'm understeering, the next I'm spinning out of control with nothing but a wall to stop me. I'm glad crashing in this game doesn't result in failure, otherwise I would've stopped within 20 minutes. I feel like this game isn't something I'll be hooked on forever though, sadly. This is only due to the fact that I'm much more interested in other genres. Anyways, don't buy this game looking for easy drifting is all I'm saying. It's challenging, yet fun!
EDIT: I've gotten about 80 minutes into the game and I've made it to the beginning of World 5. The game has a great variety of cars and customization. More than you would think it would have! I am getting the hang of the drifting and other tricks and it is now a much easier game; and it got more fun than before.
Understanding the mechanics is quite strange... it's like I'm understeering and oversteering at the same time. If you're trying to go for a long drift, don't go too hard on the gas, you will spin out very quickly. Always use the handbrake unless you're going to fast to a wall, then you should hard brake.
Anyways; this was the greatest $11 I've ever spent!
EDIT: I've got around 140 minutes into the game and I finished it. Not much replayability in my opinion. Just the same tracks and free roam courses you played in the story mode, which is quite dull if you ask me. I'm not saying I expect a huge story, but 2 hours of content? Really? Still an awfully fun game and I spend more money on things that last for 10 minutes, so I'm not complaining.

General
-------------------
Postives
- Graphics are amazing
- Not a half bad port
Negatives
- Don't like the fact it isn't all in one game, two seperate games. 1 for story/campaign and 1 for multiplayer and zombies which even you need to close the application if you want to switch from multiplayer to zombies still.
- Servers are meh
- Hackers. People that I've reported and sent evidence haven't been banned yet.
Story/Campaign
-------------------
Positives
- Generic war story, but still really enjoyable.
- Attaching characteristics
- Gameplay features (healing, getting ammo etc) is interesting
Negatives
- Short for a COD campaign
Multiplayer
-------------------
Positives
- War mode is great.
- Enjoyable doing contracts and side challenges in HQ
- Class customisation is great
- Content from loot crates are great as they're only cosmetic so micro-transaction aren't as bad (yet)
Negative
- Hackers, not a lot but they're there. Encounted 1 in lets say 3 out of 10 different lobbies. Blatent ones anyway.
- The XP rate is cut in half related to other CODs, so it takes ages to level up without double XP.
- Only 9 maps in the map rotation on normal playlists, War having 3 maps.
- If you get loot crates, prepare to be disappointment. There are so many types of grips for your pistol, you'll be getting them a lot.
- Console is more loved then PC (who would of thought after previous CODs). We don't have a Emblem Editor until 8th December and consoles already have it.
Zombies
----------------
Positives
- For first map, it's really cool and enjoyable
- Easter egg is fun, easy to do.
- Hard easter egg is challenging but is good to keep the map interesting until the new maps come out
- Hidden challenges to unlock hidden characters
- Prologue is cool
- Different types of zombies is a great variety
Negatives
-None that I can think of
Overall
The game is fun and worth a shot at playing, although I would hold of on buying season pass with it and not pay full price for it until they fix some bugs and maybe add some more content.

After hiding in the dark from this game (not watching any youtube videos) to gain my own knowledge of this game, I was wondering "Was this overhyped?"
Before I answer it, let's talk about the game. As a completely blind experience, I found learning how to play was actually surprisingly easy, and finding secrets was very fun. Gold was a useful currency, and it didn't feel very 'grindy'. Having death make you lose part of your gold made the game somewhat challenging.
The difficulty curve was quite amazing. I never found it too hard or too easy. I always found I had just enough stuff to scrape through, or I needed to go back and get something else to help along.
The items you gain are somewhat unique, and they all have their own uses. Finding out what they did never was too hard.
The upgrades never made the game amazingly easy, they just made doing things a little different.
The achievements add a lovely layer of replayability... I really have nothing else to say about that...
It's an amazing game, so, to answer the question "Was this overhyped?". OF COURSE NOT! I don't even remember the hype, I just remember people playing this game and loving it. And now, I've played it and loved it.
Why not try it out and see how you feel?

Resident Evil 5 still feels like Resident Evil, it still feels like survival horror. It just has some action sequences slapped in at the side. A lot of people hate this game, and I honestly see why. It's a very watered down co-opable version of Resi 4. But I still enjoyed it, a lot actually. It's a lot better than Resident Evil 6, that's for damn sure. It's also a great co-op game that I recommend for every co-op gamer out there. On that note, do not, I repeat, DO NOT play this game alone. The partner AI is SO BAD in this game it's not even funny. This game was built from the ground up to be a co-op game, and it clearly shows. The story is also pretty good for Resi standards.
Overall, I give Resident Evil 5 a
. Still a great game to this day. It has action sequences that shouldn't be in a Resi game, but there's not much and it's somewhat bearable, unlike Resi 6 where the entire game is filled with them.

Tbh I don't know if I should recommend this game or not...I clicked recomend because I enjoyed it (and I think my review is pretty honest so I don't want to have it masked/taken down as others seem to have been), but the thing is I cannot tell you why I liked it so much (though after 244 hours of game play I felt that I should at least try to review it). I've also experianced the errors previous reviewers have talked about so if you are worried about those I don't recommend you buy this game, though I did honestly enjoy my time (as I go onto explain).
(P.s. sorry for all the brackets I didn't really know how to start this review, but lets jump in)
MY EXPERIANCE:
At first I really hated this game, I didn't know how the layers worked or what I was doing and had to restart countless times. At one point I thought I'd quit, though because my brother had bought it and it was one of my first steam games I decided I would give one last good try.
Starting in a winter world (which is completely dominated by monsterous and powerful yeti's) my town of 20 was beaten back to just two to one-three guys (I can't remember how many probably two). Luckily they'd picked some fruits off some trees and I managed to retreat into the caves and block myself off from the Yeti outside world. Slowly I managed to turn my few fruit trees into a little cavern of food and my people were able to survive. After a while the caves became constricting and I needed to expand outside. I knew (by google) that more towns folk would only arrive if my people were happy (which they now were) and if they could actually get to my town from the corner of the map - stuck in a cave I guess this was a problem.
I managed to get my townies to avoid the Yeti's on the south-west side of the cave and I built a outdoor fenced area where I could now grow trees who needed to be on different soil and I had a gate to let new townies in.
Eventually I was able to expand my huge cave fortress across all the mountains, I had dug underground to collect armour and armour building equipment from the enemies below and I faced the yeti's in an epic battle of survival in which I won.
Skip ahead a few hours and my townies owned the map, had built a lake with a giant castle in honour of the war and a grave yard in which many brave soldiers perrished. Including my favourite townies who all had names (yes I learnt some of the names.) I continued down about 10 levels of dungeon and this is about when I started to stop playing. I guess I had quite a few goals and enemies in my game experiance and so I thoroughly enjoyed it.
THERE ARE A FEW CONS:
I'm not sure if after playing this game for so long with very little else to do I began to enjoy it, or if it was a combination of the difficulty of my original situation in the winter world and own imagination of each of my townies lives that got me to love this game. Either way I do love this game though I also understand the negative comments.
Just to clarify, I've had people die on building walls and I don't know how they got there. You have to be careful in what way things are prioritised. The AI are quite slow at building and that does rack up the hours, but you can leave it running for a while once you've got started with a bunch of tasks for them all to do. Baking is esential and so are fruits and stores and this really threw me off because people would just starve themselves out for no good reason. Sometimes when my townies had died I'd had to go back to a previous save just to figure out how and try to save them before they died again.
SUMMARY/tl;dr:
I by no means can tell you that this game is finsihed or of perfect quality, and if you're really worried about the £10 (it was cheaper when I bought it) then I wouldn't recommend it. Though what I can say, and have done a few times now, is that I really, really loved this game once I got into it. I guess the little micro managing and working out how it functions in the end made me feel a bit tallented at the game. :P

Dear Diary,
Today was my first day in EDF.
I was nervous because I have never shot a single gun before in my life, and all I ever wanted to be was to be an COBOL software engineer in a bank where I could have a steady job, a pretty wife, cute kids, and a fluffy pet Pomeranian. Unfortunately the giant ants came, and destroyed the city square where I was applying for a job, took my childhood crush away, and ate all the dogs in town.
With nowhere else to go, I went to sign up for EDF because I heard they give free packets of dried tropical fruits, in which papaya, pineapple, cempedak, and durians are my favorite. I used to eat them when I was a kid, and it would bring back childhood memories of squatting in the back of my dad's farm while flipping through his stash of pornographic memories (mammaries! ha ha ha!).
They gave me a free officer's welcome on my first day! Although it was a video on Youtube, I felt really special because they greeted us with warmth and care, and I never felt so important in my life before. We were given DVDs each to watch for weapons training, but since my DVD player is broke due to me rewinding to the special moments of Basic Instinct, I crashed my newly found EDF buddies place to have a "Weapons Training Party". We even got NERF guns to follow along with the instructional video, which I highly recommend, as it really made us feel like we were part of EDF!
I noticed that the EDF folks are really fond of yelling EDF! EDF! and I can see why. E, D and F are the easiest alphabets to read out loud in public, and the cheering of Walking Fortress BALAM while it stomped past the troops (sometimes killing some of us, but that's a small price to pay for something as awesome as BALAM). I practiced this day and night, when eating the tropical fruits, when brushing my teeth, when taking a♥♥♥♥♥♥in the loo, before I went to sleep, when talking to random girls in the bar (girls really dig the alphabets E, D and F by the way).
On the second week, we were deployed to secure the very city square that I applied for my job!!! Needless to say, I was pumped, because I really wanted to get back my USB drive containing all my special memories (mammaries! ha ha ha!) collection that I borrowed to the boss because he said that he doesn't get much sex at home due to all the weird sounds the giant ants make. The officer was really friendly, and he gave us some really sound advice : "CHARGE FORWARD FOR THE PRIDE OF EDF!!!! PICK UP AMMO OFF YOUR FRIEND'S DEAD BODIES!!!"
I got so pumped that I started practicing my special roll skill that was taught in the instructional video. With enough practice and work out, I have toned my body from man-mammaries to iron manbuns, and whenever I roll into small objects, they get destroyed now! How awesome I am, ha ha ha!
Anyway, the giant ants came, and they brought their entire family tree with them. I could tell that they brought their aunts/uncles/grandmothers/first cousin once removed/sister in law/second cousin in law once removed to the fight, but man, I pity them. If they faced any other defense force (like the Fire Defense Force, Waifu Defense Force, Mars Defense Force), they might stand a chance, but no. They faced us, the EDF!
I think I saw my new friend Bob get eaten by a giant ant but I was so caught up in the moment that couldn't help but shout EDF! EDF! EDF! while Bob became kebab by burning in the flames for the giant ants. Apart from Bob (I miss you Bob), we mowed them down with our so powerful arsenal of devastating rocket launchers, limpet guns, pistols and tropical fruits that they called out their friends, the Spiders!
I am scared of spiders ever since that day I was spanking my dolphin in the small cabin where I used to live when I was young, and one of them crawled onto my man-bone. I almost cried like a little girl when I saw the giant spiders but surprise! EDF has a spider mech of our own!!! Bob's brother in law came into action with one of them new spider mechs and blasted all the giant spiders to bits!!!
I wish I could write more but I think it's time to sweep the streets (I brought my own broom today!) to clear up the alien gibs.
TTYL Diary!

Earth defense force 4.1 is a very fun arcade shooter.  I highly recommend this game to anyone that has an interest in this game and never played it before.
There's barely any story, you go from mission to mission and the only objective is to kill all bugs in that level all the while collecting new weapons.  Each mission last about 5-10 minutes depneding on difficulty and skill level.
The controls are fairly standard for third-person shooters, WASD to move, left-click to shoot and you got some other extra keys to press for various actions, but nothing too extravagant.
There are 4 different classes you can choose from.  Each one of them has their gimmicks and special weapons, but in the end they all kill the same by blowing up bugs.
Will you get your hours worth for the current price?  Definitely.  Theres a ton of replayability in this game, gaining levels and finding stronger weapons.
The game will eventually get repetitive, but the fun is just watching all the explosions go off.  If you don't like repetitive gameplay, I would not buy this.  But if you're one that does enjoy farming, this is definitely a game for you.

Update as of 11/26/2017:
This game is still amazing. BUY TODAY!
Original Review:
Finally Earth Defense Force comes to Steam. Sure we've had Insect Armageddon but that's only an EDF game in spirit.
EDF is a very particular sort of game series. It won't appeal to everyone but for those of us who love it we REALLY love it.
The reasons people love this game (and any EDF games, for that matter):
*Distinct classes to play
*Very over the top combat scenarios (what other game has you fighting kaiju size monsters in mechs, or on foot, while getting to destroy the city around you?)
*Impressive graphics for how much is going on (It isn't the fanciest game in the world but given how much stuff is happening its very impressive they've managed to make it look and run as good as it does)
*Very addictive loot based progression
*Loads of missions
*Lots of different enemy types
*The amount of content+difficulty that extends the life of the game x4 because of the 4 separate classes and item sets
Reasons why you might not like it:
*Game can feel samey for those who don't like destructive bliss
*The campiness of the game will rub some people the wrong way
*The graphics snobs won't understand why it looks the way it does
*The difficulty can be very intimidating as you get into the later levels and higher difficulties
All in all, this is a freaking fun game. There is really nothing quite like it on Steam right now, so do yourself a favor and pick it up. If the pro/con list piqued your interest you'll probably enjoy it. And throw more money at D3 productions and Sandlot so they realize the PC market is ready for more of this awesome genre.

Surprise, surprise! Its an indie game! The best way I could describe Shovel Knight, from the perspective of someone who didn't experience the NES first hand is a case of "old dog, new tricks". This platformer harkens back to the old 8-bit style of the NES in terms of both visuals (sortof, technically, its not actually 8-bit, but whatever) and gameplay, and audio, whilst having a very modern sense of game feel at it's core.
That's the essential part, and one of the best things , in my opinion, about Shovel Knight. It could've just been a nostalgia trip, but honestly, at the core of it is an extremely well designed game that uses the basic control scheme of the NES to create an impressive level of depth (Just like some NES platformers! HOW ABOUT THAT♥♥♥♥♥♥). The spells you're given are given are all extremely fun to play and experiment with (Although, Fireballs are a bit OP).
This game feels like a kind of evolution of the 8 bit style. Story elements are told through gameplay segments that give a great sense of attention to the mainly character driven plot (Though, like 8 bit platformers, the story is quite simple, in general. It does gain some unfounded depth throughout the game, however.)
The boss battles are all amazing, with the right level of challenge leeway such that you can beat the bosses in a number of ways (No use weapon X to beat this boss a la Mega Man). the score is FANTASTIC (virt has the OST available to download, GO GET IT!). The whole package is just wonderful

If you miss the glory days of NES and SNES when platformers were king, you'll probably love this game.  The gameplay is basically a cross between the original Megaman games and Ducktales.  Your main attack is a close-range melee attack with the shovel (which you can upgrade to do a ranged attack when you have full life a la Zelda), or you can jump and do a downward "pogo stick" move with the shovel that is similar to Ducktales' cane bouncing.
Screenshots don't really do the game much justice.  The graphics on first glance look straight out of NES, but it's more of an 8-bit/16-bit hybrid, sporting a lot more colors and better animation than NES was ever capable of.  The music is also fantastic, with a majority of the tracks written by Jake Kaufman a.k.a. Virt.  He is, hands down, the best chiptune composer in the scene today.  If you like music from Capcom's NES games, you will like Shovel Knights soundtrack.
Despite the NES aesthetic, I wouldn't say the game is particularly "NES hard".  It definitely provides challenge similar to old NES games, but it's not nearly as punishing.  It doesn't have a limited number of lives or continues, and has a fair amount of checkpoints per level.  It does not give the player the futile, crushing feeling of knowing that you may never finish the game (without cheating) due to harsh life and continue limitations.  You can, however, make the game more challenging by destroying checkpoints rather than using them, and the game will reward you through other means by doing so.  There are also achievements for completing the game without dying or using any "relic" items (similar to the sub weapons in Castlevania games) for people who want a greater challenge than just finishing the game normally.
Basically, if you miss the NES/SNES days, you're missing out by not buying this game.

Rating this game is difficult because how good it is changes vastly depending on whether you are co oping or not.
Resident Evil 4 is a vastly superior singleplayer experience than this game in pretty much every way. So if you don't have an online friend who is willing to play the game together with you then get RE4 instead, or if you already played RE4 wait till this game is super cheap.

The plot is also totally ridiculous and makes any crazy characters in RE4 look normal in comparison. The problem with the game is that the plot is shown using cutscenes and diary entries, both bad ideas when you are in an online co op game. It would have been better off told during normal gameplay. Even so, it's nothing worth reading because it's so insipid. It has every cliche in the book and totally rips off stuff like the Matrix. The setting is also not much better, while starting out in Africa it soon progresses to areas that make zero practical sense in terms of why they are there.
It gets a thumbs down for singleplayer, so only play if there's someone willing to play it with you unless you can get it on sale/bundle.

I'm so happy a Sandlot developed EDF game has come to the PC.
The last EDF game I got to play was EDF2017 on the Xbox 360.
I quickly fell in love with that game. Many hours were spent playing it coop
with my brother- diagonal rolling, shooting giant ants, spiders, and robots
and collecting loot drops hoping to unlock the best weapons.
Griefing eachother with ridiculously explosive grenades (that have
a blast radius so large it's impossible to throw it without killing yourself).
Leveling entire cities with rocket launchers.
The game was pure fun.
And now there's EDF 4.1, and it's 2017 but better in every way.
No more frame rate drops - it's a constant smooth 60fps at 1440p.
No more 2D sprites for weapon, health, and armor drops, they're 3D now and fit the environments much better.
Graphics, while simple, look great. Particularly the lighting effects (eg. the flashlight actually matters in cave levels now).
Great mouse and keyboard controls - shooting feels precise and smooth.
More ridiculous weapons!
Split screen Coop on PC!
4-player online coop! I played for 2 hours in a full room and it ran without a hitch (note: I really like the way text chat is done during gameplay).
4 classes with unique playstyles (whereas EDF2017 only had one class).
It's the EDF I know and love, only more of it and in a smoother and more polished package.
And I couldn't be happier. 10/10.
Thanks for porting this, Sandlot!!

This coming out on steam really caught me by surprise!
I have a combined 500+ hours of this game on ps3 and ps4, and the only major thing that detracted from this series was the framerate drops. Well, now that's gone. So this game is pretty much perfect now, for me.
Shadow of New Despair has a ton of content, a lot more than before the ps4 revision, and even on the ps3 it had plenty of content, so if you want a time sink, this is it.
As far as the class balancing goes, i've seen a decent amount of all classes in my time on ps3-4. So far on here i haven't seen any wing divers, oddly. It might just be me. More importantly, each class compliments the other, with plenty of synergies and weapon combinations. On harder difficulties you actually HAVE TO think about how all of your squads weapons will work together to prevent being overtaken by a hoarde of insects. To me playing in a squad of four really boosts this game into another realm for me; there are just so many possibilities and different ways to play for each and every level that it just blows me away every time.

The best fishing sim I've played. Not perfect, but absolutely better than the competition.
Pros:
Immensely diverse range of tackle, gear and baits. This is kind of a double edged sword as the depth of options makes for a steep learning curve; selecting the right gear for the right species is problematic, especially for starting  players. One needs only to take note of the subject matter within the in game chat channel--this almost invariably consists of players asking 'which hook/leader length/area do I need to catch X fish'. That said, I don't think the brevity of tackle options should be considered a negative. This balanced a little bit by the number of guides and info videos available online--most of what you need to learn can be gathered pretty handily outside of the game.
There is a wide vvariety of fish to taget and while most do share similar rig preferences, there's still enough nuance required in order to land trophy and unique specimens which makes for good challenges.Calender events serve as a way for players to catch fantasy fish which are worth fair amounts of in-game currency, which can be used to purchase the best gear and baits. Nothing is locked behind a paywall, although special offers do come along seasonally which gives people the option to purchase extremely high end gear at lower levels--in this sense, the game is technically pay to win. Fighting fish is a fun, and unlike Euro Fishing, the physics which govern these are intuitive and intelligible;  striking, reeling and lure retrieval mechanics are all well concieved  and work consistently, and solidly. The graphics are pretty good for an in dev game, ambient noise is realistic, and the locales are pretty enough to look at.
Cons:
Perhaps ironically, Fishing Planet is possibly too realistic. Missed strikes, incorrect rig, lure and bait choices can result in lots of time spent winding or watching a float bob for no result. It pays to do your  research before heading out. It is also quite grindy; levelling is slow especially in the teens, and this is exacerbated by the fact that gear access is level restricted. In order to catch fish which yield worthwhile cash and experience  relative to your level, you often find yourself needing gear you can't access. The result is that you wind up grinding out fish which are no challenge to catch, and yield little rewards and experience.It's a bit off kilter and hopefully the devs correct this in the future as this is probably the biggest, and most monotonous flaw in the game.
As far as I can tell, unique and trophy fish seem to drop at inconsistent rates depending on the species. Trophy catfish in the starting area are common, yet you can expect to reel in dozens of bass before landing a trophy specimen. Post patch, alligator gar have become impossibly rare, whereas unique redear sunfish are caught hand over fist. It's a broekn system which requires an overhaul.
Overall, and  considering that Fishing Planet is pre-release, it's definitely well worth playing. The foundations for something great are all there, It just needs some refinement. And there's enough to keep you interested in the interim.

There's a ton of SUPER RETRO 8-BIT INDIE GAMES out there, but if any of them get it right, its Shovel Knight.
I have trouble thinking of problems with this game. I'm of the opinion that indie developers fall back on pixel graphics because they aren't capable or knowledgable in creating art beyond that. But Shovel Knight takes pride in it; its art isn't lazy, its extremely good and clearly down by highly skilled artists restricting themselves to pixels, rather than the other way around. It has every right to have its retro graphics, and its excellent character design, detail, and art overall shows that its not falling back on pixel graphics to draw its audience, but because it looks good. I almost wish for a world where indie games
have that stigma, so Shovel Knight can shine in its own way.
The only issue I can come up with for this game is it loses itself just slightly near the end: The last few levels are lacking in a number of ways, as they're not really unique and don't feature anything design wise as brilliant and clever as every single level before it. As an example, each level features a miniboss and a couple of short but cleverly utilized gimmicks throughout that are still never the focus of the entire level. The final few levels have neither, at all. They're not challenging either, though they try to be by having large amounts of spikes and endless bottomless pits. The final boss is also quite easy. Still, it did end satisfyingly, and I would never say these issues were as bad as other games that take a total dive near the end.
The developers were aware they were full of talent and don't hesitate to put every bit of heart they have into it, in general.
I fought every bonus boss (4 of them) and completed every bonus level (several, maybe 8 or so) and ended up with 9-10 hours, with a New Game+ ahead, so at $15 you're getting a way better deal than any modern AAA title clocking in at 10 hours you can think of. DLC for lots of good stuff is on its way too.

A simple concept beautifully exectued. Casual and relaxing but also competetive if you're in that mood. The minimalistic graphics and relaxing music creates a very likeable atmosphere (Mirror's Edge comes to mind). The controls are fluid and the physics surprisingly good, which makes the game challenging but also rewarding when you nail a run. There are some annoying bugs, but nothing major. The sound goes wonky sometimes but a restart of the event fixes it and for some reason the car is in reverse at the start of a race occasionally.
"Story mode" is very brief and contains tutorials for the different race modes and simple missions. Missions are repetitive (spin here, do donuts around that, drift through here) and you'll spend a lot of time driving around trying to find the last ones to unlock the next area. I wouldn't recommend this game for the price if you're just going to play through the free roam mode as the content just isn't there. But if you enjoy perfecting your skills there's a lot of replay value and leaderboards to climb. There are three modes: track, mountain pass and gymkhana and quite a few locations for each.
Unfortunatley there seems like some cheating or exploiting exists as some high scores on certain tracks are outright impossible to achieve (I've seen scores ten times higher than second place) but unless you're able to score in the top 3 or so this won't affect you much.
Still, overall a very enjoyable and well executed game. I hope to see more from the developer.

This is an absolutely perfect addition to the Portal universe. First, the game looks fantastic, capturing a whole new side of Aperture we haven't seen before. In the introductory sequence in which you enter Aperture on a Half Life style monorail, it paints the picture of a fully functioning Old Aperture exactly as I imagined it being based on what we saw in Portal 2. Then, the inevitable happens, the test your character, Mel, is taking part in is a failure, and you wake up in the now decayed remains of Old Aperture, and have to make your way back up and out to the surface.
All the while, you're solving puzzles that are challenging, starting right off the bat with the first few tests. This game shows no mercy! Admittedly, some of the puzzles are a bit too challenging at times (two test chambers in particular), and took me far too long to solve, frustrating me and taking me out of the experience. But for the most part, while challenging, the puzzles are incredibly fun to solve!
Then, you have the voice acting, which is an achievement in itself: AEGIS, Virgil, Cave Johnson, all very well done! I'll admit, it did take me some time to get used to the Cave Johnson impression in the beginning of the game, but it's actually quite good! And with regards to capturing what I feel is the essence of the personality of Cave that we know from Portal 2, the game's writers got it just about perfect.
The writer's also did an exceptional job with the dialogue for your guide, the personality core Virgil. Virgil is a very appropriate name for your guide, by the way. Virgil, in Dante's Divine Comedy, is the guide who walks with Dante as he traverses through Hell and Purgatory and similarly the Virgil in this game walks you through the "hell" that is now the Aperture facility. Not sure if that's why they chose the name Virgil, but that's pretty cool if it is!
And then there's the music, which perfectly captures the atmosphere of Aperture. The last song after you leave Aperture ("Decades of Science" on the soundtrack) actually gave me chills, as the camera panned over the ruins of Aperture.
All in all, a very welcome addition to the Portal universe and hopefully one day will be considered part of the Portal canon. I can't recommend this game enough. If you're a fan of the Portal games, this is something you absolutely need to play! Considering that this game is approximately 6-8 hours of play time for one playthrough, it would absolutely be worth paying for, but since it's free, there's no excuse to not play it!

Resident Evil 5 isn't a survival horror game, but that doesn't mean it hasn't learned a great deal from the genre. Tension is the central element of survival horror games, and in the past it has been conveyed by the gloomy settings, the sense of isolation, and the frustratingly clunky camera angles and controls--all RE5 does differently is convey this feeling through other outlets. Having a partner introduces new types of tension, because you're forced to rely on each other's support, find ways to manage both of your inventories during battles, and cover larger areas since enemies can appear from almost anywhere. Waves of enemies wax and wane with just the right frequency, and while the brightly lit environments make them less scary, they can be tough to deal with because they attack in large numbers and are smarter, faster, and stronger than their counterparts in previous games. Major encounters and boss fights are doled out with excellent pacing, and since you're never sure what to expect around the corner, you have to remain vigilant. The active inventory management system helps keep that anxiety up as well.

How to Steam Potatoes
Steamed potatoes are easy, quick, and best of all, delicious.
Prep Time: 5 minutes
Cook Time: 30 minutes
Total Time: 35 minutes
Servings: 6
Ingredients:
28-32 ounces small baby potatoes, such as baby Yukon gold or red potatoes
2 tablespoons butter, melted (1 ounce; 28 grams)
Kosher Salt
Fresh or dried herbs
Instructions:
1) Wash potatoes. Add about one-inch of water to a pot that has a fitted steamer basket or can hold a steamer insert.
2) Place potatoes into steamer basket. Cover pot. Turn pot to high. When steam starts to escape from the lid, reduce heat to medium, about ten minutes.
3) Steam until potatoes are tender, about 30 minutes. Time varies depending on the size of the potatoes.
Transfer potatoes to a medium bowl. Pour melted butter over potatoes. Stir. Season with kosher salt and herbs to taste.

As for difficulty the game does not seem to have a set way of selcting diffuclty but seems to go the route of it is easy at first but as you pass each level the game gets gradually harder.
The game has NO MOUSE CONTROL, this is not a issue as the Keyboard works just fine although it is a bit odd at first, I do reccomend that you completely redo the keybinds, I personally set mine so that I used WASD to move and the arrow keys to attack/use Relic/change Relic and this seems to work well.
The game does have more to offer than the typical 8-bit Paltformer, you have armor upgrades, Relic upgrades, HP upgrades, and Mana upgrades to make your character more capable at keep up with the level progression. There are cities which you can visit to speak to NPC's to purchase these upgrades and items. The items work entirley off in game gold which is aquired by find trasure collecting coins and most importantly dying as little as possible as you lose Gold each time you die.
The story does not seem to "pull you in" but it is enough story to make you understand the importance of what your doing and to slightly attach yourself to the main character and make you symphosize with him. *NO SPOILERS HERE* The gist of the story is that you where at one point a great warrior/adventurer who was well known and protected people from evil doers, as your companion there was a female knight named Shield Knight and you and her were a "thing". One day she got killed by a dark enchantress, her death leads to the Shovel Knight retiring to enjoy the last of his days in solitude. As time passes the dark Enchantress takes over the area and has numerous henchmen spread around the area. You have decided to get your revenge and step into the battle and take down the Enchanteress and free the area.
All in all the game is a lot of fun, it is very hard to stop playing once you have started. There are lots of hidden treasures. bosses, and areas which are not mandatory but will offer many different types of rewards. I would reccomend this to a friend and am glad I bought this game!
-Xodas

As Frustrating As You Probably Don't Remember
I wanted to write this just to provide an alternative perspective to the mostly gushing reviews this game has enjoyed. First off, most of what those glowing reviews say is true: this game replicates the look and sound of the classic 8-bit games flawlessly. The enemies are varied, and you'll probably recognize many of the archetypes from a game you used to play as a child. Same goes for the level design; the sliding platforms and fire-spitting hatches are all there, just as you left them.
That said, the game carries over the flaws of that bygone generation. You die, a lot. The further in you go, the game demands more split-second precision, shovel-fulls of luck, and a masochistic desire for repetition. The bosses require learning their every move while dying a lot. Then they require practicing your motions while dying a lot. Then they require executing your motions while trying not to die. By the time I completed a level I felt more frustration than satisfaction, just wanting to quit. Thankfully, a "Quit to Desktop" button is one modern creation which was implemented here. The frustration is one of those things you may not remember about those old games. Shovel Knight brings those memories right back.
What I'm trying to say is that this game is not for everyone, and that sometimes nostalgia is best left as a memory. This game is a creation that faithfully recreates the 8-bit era, adopting its triumphs and failures. Back in the day as a child, and with no alternatives, I may have had a higher pain threshold(and free time) to see these games through, but not any more. My own realization was that my nostalgia is not worth paying for this replica, and re-living those frustrations. However, if you really do want to relive the NES experience, why not just get an emulator and play the originals?

Many horror games claim to be scary, but none of them have terrified my like Amnesia. While other games try to scare you with over-the-top gore and things jumping out at you, Amnesia takes a more cerebral approach. Little things like the sound of footsteps, or a door just barely hanging open are enough to freak you out. Sure, there are horrifying enemies, and they'll make you pee your pants, but what really gets you is the constant anxiety of wondering what's around every corner. And when you do encounter something, the sense of fear and helplessness is overwhelming.
However, this is a game you should not miss out on. The developers make a point to space out the fear with (relatively) calm, yet creepy puzzles. Definitely a great game to play around friends.
Would recommend this game if it wasn't unfinished.

After playing the very disappointing DS version of Plants vs. Zombies, this PC version feels and plays great.
When I heard about PvZ the very first time when I was like 8, I watched ZackScottGames play it, and loved it. A tower defense game that I was really looking forward to play when I realized it's on the DS, and got it on Christmas. When I started playing, I was really disappointed, but I forced myself to finish it since I got it. I finished it in about a week, and it was hell. The graphics did look good for the DS, and using a touchscreen made it easy to place plants and collect sun/money. Other than that, the framerate was awful when Waves happen (Can go from decent to like 5 fps), a good amount of small bugs, the Multiplayer was a bust, and the funny zombie animations weren't there (Like for example: when a zombie gets blown up on the PC version, they turn black and turn to dust. On the DS version, they just turn black and disappear.). So much was so downgraded in the DS version it wasn't even funny, and for 40 dollars? No thanks.
8-9 years after that train-wreak, I got the PC version when it was on sale, and it's so much better and more enjoyable.
Okay, on to the real review:
Plants vs. Zombies is a Tower-Defense game where you need to use plants in order to defend your home from zombies. In order to plant your plants, you need Sun. In order to get Sun, you can plant Sunflowers to increase the amount of Sun you can get, or just wait (planting Sunflowers is the best idea at the start.). Once you get enough Sun for a plant you want to plant (Example: Peashooter), you can select that plant, and place it into an available spot on the lawn.
It's simplistic, yes, but it gets challenging as eff in later levels.
At level 1-# and 2-#, you are at your lawn. The lawn is the easiest, since it's only 5 lanes, and you don't need a special plant in order to fully secure all the lanes (exept on 2-#). Level 3-# and 4-# is the backyard. The backyard is harder, since you have 6 lanes, and the 2 lanes in the middle are water lanes. You need Lily Pads in order to place plants on the water. Level 3-# isn't all that bad, and does take a bit to get use to, but on Level 4-#, you need to know what you are doing. Fog takes up half of the right of the screen, and you need a special plant in order to get rid of some of the fog. You don't know where a zombie is at or what lane it's in, because the fog blocks the view.  Level 5-# and 6-# are the hardest levels of them all. It all takes place on your bloody roof, which means there is no ground for your plants. You need a special plant, which is the Flower Pot. Flower Pots can be placed on the roof, and you can plant a plant on it. What makes it so hard? Flower Pots cost Sun in order to place down, and there is 7 lanes, so it will take a lot of time to save up a lot of Sun for Flower Pots and plants. Not only that, but in Level 5-# and 6-#, they use the strongest zombies in the game. It makes things much more challenging. You have to be fast, and you need to know what you are doing. The final level in the game is the final boss, which I won't spoil at all. At level 1/3/5-#, it's daylight, which means you can get Sun from the sky, but at 2/4/6-#, you don't get Sun from the sky, meaning that you can only get Sun from your plants.
There is a ton of different zombies in the game. There is the normal one, which are easy as hell, Conehead Zombies, which take two Peashooters to kill, Ironbucket Zombies, which takes 3 Peashooters, Football Zombies, which needs some really good defense to kill, Disco Zombies, which summons zombies when he poses and just as strong as the Coneheads, and much, much more. It keeps the game fresh and doesn't make it dull after the very first Levels.
There is a ton of different plants to choose in the game as well. There is over 25 different plants to choose, and you unlock one at the end on almost every level. Sunflowers are your friend, and will always be in this game.
Even though there is a lot of plants to choose from, the game doesn't really hold your hand when it comes to choosing at the start at almost every level. You can only hold up 6 plants to choose from, and you can buy more at Crazy Dave's store. So that means you need to think when you do your choices, as it can backfire.
Speaking of Crazy Dave's store, you can buy upgrades and other things when you are in Levels. In order to buy items, you need to get Crazy Dave's keys (which is in 3-5, I think), and you need to save up money for the items (coins are dropped sometimes when zombies are killed.). If you have enough money, you can buy that item, and can use it in the Level. It's quite useful.
I know there is more to the game, but I want you to try it out, and see what the game has to offer. For 5 dollars, it's worth it!
But I did have some flaws with the PC version:
It needs Co-op, like on the console versions. Playing alone by yourself is fun, but playing the game with a friend makes it a blast to play. If it was Vs. Multiplayer (like the DS version.), then no thanks.
Wish you can skip the tutorial at the start of the game, because the tutorial is just boring to play.
TL;DR, I really recommend it! If you love Tower-Defense games, or a game that will give good entertainment or a good laugh, this is for you! The gameplay is great stuff. Get it on PC, not on the DS.
Final Scores:
DS: 3/10
PC: 9/10

This game is amazing.  It not only successfully replicates the aesthetic and design philosphies of the 8bit era games that it's paying homage to (primarily Mega Man) but it manages to, in my opinion, be straight up better than those games in nearly every way.
Even if you found titles like Mega Man 2 to be too archaic for whatever reason, Shovel Knight adds in enough modern convenience through the likes of intelligently placed checkpoints to allow practically anyone to succeed.  For those wanting a more traditional challenge, you can manually destroy those checkpoints to get bonus gold - a great example of scalable difficulty.
The audio visual aesthetic is sublime - it does its best effort to stay within the confines of the NES's hardware while cheating slightly to expand upon the color pallette and allow environmental/lighting effects.  If you're even remotely fond of chiptune music, the OST here should be enough reason for you to check this title out.
Seriously, just pick this title up.  Only downside is it's quite short - taking around 4-6 hours for a playthrough.

After finishing Resident Evil 4 I jumped straight into Resident Evil 5, and althought maybe not quite as good as the 4th game I still enjoyed it.
The story this time starts with Chris arriving in Africa and meeting up with his new partner for the mission, Sheva. Things take a turn for the worse fast, and you end up having to shoot your way through hordes of Majini (zombies), monsters, as well as certain "old friends".
Having watched the Resident Evil movies before playing this game I already knew most of the "twists", which kind of sucked, so if you plan on playing this game I recommend that you
watch the most recent Resident Evil movies first (if you haven't already). The movies are pretty bad to begin with, and having them ruin parts of the story is not worth it.
The gameplay this time around focuses mostly on shooting your way through hordes of enemies, and I'm not sure if I would call this game a survival horror game at all. Many of the missions take place during the day in fairly open areas, so it's pretty must just a 3rd person action shooter. That said, it's a pretty
action shooter, so as long as you know what to expect you will probably get alot of enjoyment out of this game. Just be prepared for the idiot AI partner to get (you) killed alot unless you have someone to play co-op with.
There was one mission, the extra mission Lost in Nightmares, which felt like a real survival horror game, and it even takes place in the Spencer mansion from the original game, so make sure you don't miss this mission if you decide to play this game.
So far I have enjoyed all the Resident Evil games that I have played, this one being no exception, so I definitely recommend it to both fans (with an open mind) of the Resident Evil series as well as fans of 3rd person shooters.
Just a warning to people (like me) who care about achievements. There are a couple of very grindy multiplayer achievements in this game, some of which require 4 players to be online at the same time, and since the multiplayer is pretty much dead you might have a hard time clearing everything. I managed to do it in the end, but it was a real pain. The DLC is also required to clear the game 100%. You have been warned.

Short Version:  AMAZING!
Verbose Version:
Shovel Knight is, hands-down, the most amazing new platformer game I've played in years.  Try it - I'm absolutely certain you'll feel the same!  If you're like me and grew up in the NES era, then your entire 3+ decade experience with video games is informed by those early titles.  Personally, I love the new and the old, playing the latest AAA productions in one moment, and retro system classics the next.  If you can identify with that, then you simply must put aside your Steam gaming backlog for a moment, and give yourself an evening to play Shovel Knight.  It has been awhile since a new title has compelled me to play straight through from beginning to end, but I was instantly gripped and can't wait to play *again* in NG+.
Shovel Knight is clearly made by a team who knows this genre inside and out, and have produced a masterpiece that combines a unique cast of characters/abilities/equipment, perfect responsive controls (d-pad FTW, and if you play on a TV, best to mitigate any input lag!), beautiful visuals, top-notch music, superb writing, retro references galore, and every other possible indication that the creation of this title was a labour of love.  Honestly - I can't fault anything about it.  Shovel Knight is completely endearing to me, and my heart-felt congratulations go out to the team at Yacht Club Games - anybody who was a part of creating this has true reason to feel proud.  I will be watching this studio closely in the future.
If you were ever a fan of any of the Mega Man, Castlevania, Super Mario Brothers, Ninja Gaiden, Contra, or Duck Tales games, then Shovel Knight is for you.  Or if you missed that generation and haven't caught up through virtual console, but enjoyed Dark Souls or any of the new Rayman games, again, it's a must play.
