游戏的屏幕截图：车辆爆炸，环境挑战进度显示在右边
这个系列历史上被认为是侠盗猎车手[11] [13]的一个克隆，后来将它定位为比较“更高兴地愚蠢”。[11] [18]在战斗中，玩家从武器选择轮[19] [c]中选择武器，包括普通手枪，冲锋枪，猎枪和火箭发射器以及诸如无人机和无人机眩晕手榴弹等特殊武器。玩家近战攻击包括运行攻击如DDT和紫色假阳具蝙蝠。[20]玩家可以使用车辆导航城市，包括一个悬停喷气式飞机（被称为F-69垂直起降）和一个像素化的后期坦克，通过故事任务解锁。一旦特殊车辆被解锁，它们是无限供应的，并且可以直接传递到玩家角色的位置。[13]玩家的行动加剧了Volition称为“真棒按钮”，例如，玩家将通过挡风玻璃进入汽车的司机座位。[19]主要故事运动任务可以单独或合作地在线或通过System Link离线播放。[13] [d]一些元素被添加到第二个播放器的活动。[20]没有竞争的多人游戏，但是一个“波浪为基础的生存模式”称为♥♥♥♥♥d模式[11]，最多支持两个玩家。[21]
玩家在介绍任务后自定义角色。玩家角色身体，衣服和车辆可以定制，[13] [e]以及家庭财产。玩家还可以在Saints Row在线社区中分享他们的角色设计。[20]除了主要故事任务，还有可选择的转移，赚取钱和赢得声誉，如保险欺诈，玩家伤害自己在交通量最大化自己的伤害，在定时器到期前，或Mayhem，玩家最大限度地破坏财产的时间到期。这些转换中的一些是在之前的圣徒游戏中引入的。[13] [f]活动服务于情节，被定位为训练玩家角色或破坏团体。[19]他们也可以重复。[15]在结构化转换之外，玩家可以通过购买物业，购买物品，寻找隐藏的性玩偶和钱缓存收藏品，以及主动肆虐的破坏来自由娱乐。[14]还有“闪点”帮派操作，当中断时给予尊重。[17]攻击他人会增加玩家的臭名声，如星星所描绘的。

Although it may not have the super-stellar visual effects of some other games (the 'you're-going-crazy' effect can be a little cheesy and let's be honest, no one has furniture that matches that perfectly!) and it's about as single-player as you can get, this game is fantastically fun to play. The puzzles have the right amount of 'challenging' to be fun, but not so much that it's too frustrating. The game provides you with limited resources that you're required to use, and plays on less-used aspects of 'survival horror.' You don't WANT to use the items you've got (no player does, you're saving them after all!) where they'll be wasted, but you're going to HAVE to use them, and that makes you anxious and worried. ("What if I needed that more later?)
Still images don't do it justice. You really have to see it in action and be behind the controls to get the full experience- on a dark night, with all the lights off, this game can be incredibly immersive.

I think it's easy to be dismissive of games that look like Shovel Knight in 2014; "oh great, yet another pixel art game". But to do so would be to miss out on a very enjoyable platformer with it's roots firmly in the NES era.
The controls are tight, the writing is really good and, for the cost, there's a lot of content there (my playthrough took 8 hours - although your milage may vary as I'm a little out of practice!).
Shovel Knight is a reminder why platformers on the NES are so well thought of, it's an homage without ever getting over-bearing and has a terrific difficulty curve to it, providing some real challenge in the later levels (although those used to Spelunky, Super Meat Boy and co will probably disagree).
So all in all, Shovel Knight is a game that's really easy to like and recommend.

Evolution is a critical part in the existance of the world. As time goes by circumstances change and species either adapt or go extinct.
is all about evolution, both in content and in gameplay. It might not be what you want it be, but it works.
is branded as the black sheep of the Resident Evil franchise. It is the installment where everything went overboard and everything that made Resident Evil,
was replaced with elements that made it
.
is a third person shooter at heart and not a survival horror game. This polarised many fans of the series. Even at its darkest,
isn't scary. Unsettling at best, but you're so stacked on ammo and firepower at all times that you'll be hard pressed to actually fear for your life. So, in short, you'll be gunning your way through posessed villagers, various monsters and a broad assortment of bosses; and it is very enjoyable to do so.
The game drops you, Chris Redfield,
allumni, and Sheva Alomar, series newcomer and dark horse, in Africa where you're tasked to apprehend an arms dealer. Things quickly escalate when bio-weapons are involved and they're stronger and more advanced than anything seen before. The story proceeds to wrap up the ends brought forth in the earlier installments and pits you against an old enemy whose voice is arguably the sexiest baritone ever to grace the airwaves. The presentation and pace help sell the completely insane plot. If you're not an initated follower of
then you'll be dumbfounded. However, if you're in on the mania, than be prepared for a turbulent and explosive ride.
Gameplay is fast and agressive. The combat system actively encourages to get your hands dirty. And since you're accompanied by an AI partner, or possible coop player, you'll be dishing out pain left and right. The AI's aim is to be commended. While their inventory management leaves something to be desired, the computer player knows when to shoot and it makes it count. It helps you get past some of the more frustrating moments that much easier, allowing you to get back to work asap. And you'll be doing work. The shooting from
is back, but the enemies are more resiliant and they want your fist in their face. Chris' enormous biceps are going to show their worth when you get the hang of it.
is a violent and agressive evolution of the game that
was. It isn't as revolutionary and some parts are bound to rub you the wrong way, but it is fun game to play. The viceral violence, the story and level design all add up to something really cool. Add to that some of the best action set pieces ever since they became a thing and you have a recipe for success.

Those of you who're thinking of buying this game because you played and enjoyed RE4, turn around and walk away now. Let me explain to you why RE5 is NOTHING compared to RE4.
I enjoyed RE4 immensely, I've played it hours and completed it 100% on all difficulties. After reading a few (in hindsight VERY MISLEADING) reviews, thought I'd enjoy RE5 as well. But boy was I wrong.
First of all, there's no story. Or nearly no story. You just go from A to B and shoot things. Don't expect an intriguing story like I did, having played RE4 before. After a few chapters it'll get very repetitive.
Also, there's no creepy, scary feel to the game. Everything seems to be in broad daylight, there wasn't even a single point in the game that I was hesitant/too scared to progress. Just run and shoot, easy.
Second, while the overall controls are similar to RE4, which I like, they now put in a HORRIBLE inventory system. Not only does it look and feel very very cheap and unfinished, it's more of a hassle than an additional challenge of good inventory management, like it was in RE4.
Third, the bosses and enemies are just, so, boring. It's like they used the least imaginative, probably cheapest, artists to create the monsters and bosses. Just expect slimy black tentacles. Yey.
And I could've accepted this boring monster-design fact, if these bosses would at least prove a challenge to kill. But no, they threw in gatling guns everywhere to kill the bosses. You don't even have to rely on your gunmanship skills anymore, you just point and shoot with the gatling gun. YAWN.
Fourth, I expect they ran out of ideas, because they just filled in some levels with vehicles: drive a jeep and shoot a gatling gun. Urgh. Steer a ship and shoot a gatling gun. Sigh. Stand on a deck and shoot a gatling gun. Whoop.
Fifth: there aren't any cool weapons in this game. Each weapon feels like you're holding a toy gun, they don't sound good, they don't look good. And the upgrades aren't interesting like they were in RE4, because there aren't even exclusive upgrades anymore when maxing out your gun!
The only thing I really enjoyed in this game is the melee attacks you can perform with your buddy online. Stun an enemy, punch him in the face. And if it's a stronger enemy, you can both unleash your melee actions on it, for even greater damage. Aaand that's really about the only positive thing I have to say about this game.
So I think I'm clear: RE4 fans, don't do this to yourself, don't buy this game. Even the multiplayer, which is the reason why I bought this game, doesn't make up for all it's flaws.
It's like a mental cringe, each time you discover how bad it is compared to RE4. It's a waste of money.

MAKE SURE YOU PLAY THE ADVANCED SERIES INSTEAD OF STORY MODE
Summary of my spoiler-free review of Story Mode:
- EXCELLENT map design
- Good puzzles but some have obvious flaws
- Good music, but not on it's own
- Okay writing (sometimes great, sometimes forced)
- Decent voice acting
I recommend this game to everyone who enjoyed Portal 2 - the shortcommings are nit-picks and won't detract from the experience too much. Additionally, many of my complaints are fixed in the advanced series.
Play as Mel as you explore old aperture before being cryosleep'd into a time period between Portal 1 and 2. The map design is outsatnding, there is eyecandy and subtle humor everywhere and a lot of areas to look at and explore, all throughout the game. The quality of the maps are on par with Portal 2 if not better, making this feel like it could have been a true Portal 1.5. However, some of the other aspects aren't on par - some of the puzzle designs have some obvious exploits that let you skip massive parts of the puzzle easily, and other puzzles have testing elements that I found completely unneccesary, as if they were red herrings (intended to not be used) which doesn't make much sense. The difficulty of the puzzles is on par with Portal 2, maybe slightly harder, which was a little dissappointing to me, HOWEVER most of the puzzles were very enjoyable because they were fizzler puzzles. For those that don't know, fizzler puzzles are very enjoyable (at least for me). One of the new testing elements is a fizzler that also kills you, so it's like a laser wall that doesn't alow objects through...in other words, it's a piece of glass that can be turned off, which already exists in Portal 2 (that jump suit you're wearing looks stupid). Something cool though is the use of water to put out fires, though it feels like a gimmick. The music isn't as energetic as Portal 2, it's actually more along the lines of Portal 1 as it is eerie and mysterious while also being very robotic. I wouldn't listen to it outside the context of this game but it felt appropriate and is well made. Finally, the dialog/writing - some of the jokes are very funny, but most of the time it feels like they are trying to repeat existing jokes from Portal 2, mostly the ones that became memes. It felt forced and it wasn't done very well in my opinion. Also unusual is that a character at first says GLaDOS's name, but then every time later they say "HER" instead. It feels weird, as if the character I was with was suddenly swapped out with Wheatley. There's even a copy of the neurotoxin hacking scene from Portal 2, except that instead of thinking with portals, you just press a button. As for voice acting, the Cave Johnson actor didn't feel very natural to me - not because it didn't sound like Cave Johnson, but because of the meme repitition I mentioned earlier. It felt like I was listening to a remix of Cave Johnson quotes. The other characters in the game are done well, though, and I felt like they were really there. If you liked Portal 2, then you should definitely play this game as you will enjoy it too. My criticisms are nit-picks and despite them the game is still great and it's clear a lot of effort went into every aspect.

The soundtrack of this game will bring you to tears, bring purpose to your life, and encourage you for you to do your best in not just this game, but in life itself. Yes, this game has a practical, real life message to send to all. Many assumed that our dear friend who gifted us this glorious new art form was a typical joker. It is a shame I can only recommend this game positively, as, if steam allowed it, I would set my steam profile to redirect any viewers to the store page of this game. Those of you who're thinking of buying this game because you played and enjoyed RE4, turn around and walk away now. Let me explain to you why RE5 is NOTHING compared to RE4.
I enjoyed RE4 immensely, I've played it hours and completed it 100% on all difficulties. After reading a few (in hindsight VERY MISLEADING) reviews, thought I'd enjoy RE5 as well. But boy was I wrong.
First of all, there's no story. Or nearly no story. You just go from A to B and shoot things. Don't expect an intriguing story like I did, having played RE4 before. After a few chapters it'll get very repetitive.
Also, there's no creepy, scary feel to the game. Everything seems to be in broad daylight, there wasn't even a single point in the game that I was hesitant/too scared to progress. Just run and shoot, easy.
Second, while the overall controls are similar to RE4, which I like, they now put in a HORRIBLE inventory system. Not only does it look and feel very very cheap and unfinished, it's more of a hassle than an additional challenge of good inventory management, like it was in RE4.
Third, the bosses and enemies are just, so, boring. It's like they used the least imaginative, probably cheapest, artists to create the monsters and bosses. Just expect slimy black tentacles. Yey.
And I could've accepted this boring monster-design fact, if these bosses would at least prove a challenge to kill. But no, they threw in gatling guns everywhere to kill the bosses. You don't even have to rely on your gunmanship skills anymore, you just point and shoot with the gatling gun. YAWN.
Fourth, I expect they ran out of ideas, because they just filled in some levels with vehicles: drive a jeep and shoot a gatling gun. Urgh. Steer a ship and shoot a gatling gun. Sigh. Stand on a deck and shoot a gatling gun. Whoop.
Fifth: there aren't any cool weapons in this game. Each weapon feels like you're holding a toy gun, they don't sound good, they don't look good. And the upgrades aren't interesting like they were in RE4, because there aren't even exclusive upgrades anymore when maxing out your gun!
The only thing I really enjoyed in this game is the melee attacks you can perform with your buddy online. Stun an enemy, punch him in the face. And if it's a stronger enemy, you can both unleash your melee actions on it, for even greater damage. Aaand that's really about the only positive thing I have to say about this game.
So I think I'm clear: RE4 fans, don't do this to yourself, don't buy this game. Even the multiplayer, which is the reason why I bought this game, doesn't make up for all it's flaws.
It's like a mental cringe, each time you discover how bad it is compared to RE4. It's a waste of money.

This is one of the best games I have ever played. It is extremely well polished and designed game (in both its levels and its bosses), has beautiful graphics that really give that throwback feel and playstyle, has one of the best soundtracks for a game, its original and new, and its simply a masterpiece. I had so much fun with this game and it has such a great replayability that I will probably see myself playing this as many times as possible till I get all the achievements.
Its design flows, levels don't require any sort of backtracking or tedious traversing, and it uses elements of the game that are familiar to old gamer veterans who played games like megaman and other side scrollers. Its compact yet big enough to get a sense to explore, and attempt to find treasure and goal. It has that castlevania/megaman feel in which you traverse a level, find special weapons and upgrades along the way, and maybe you can use it against the boss, or it just helps with traversing the level or overall making you stronger. They don't lay everything out for you and you get a sense of acomplishment when you find something new and you inivate a strategy for using it. First playthrough I didn't even use all the items, I simply collected them for the sake of completion and exploration. Its balanced, not too hard and not too easy (could have a bit more challenging bosses though, but then a no die playthrough would be absolute torture :P) The design is fun and flows that it is actually fun to get to the boss as you gotta solve mini puzzles and figure out how to traverse to the next platform.
The style fits for that throwback feel and sidescroller action that is implemented in games like megaman which bring back that feeling of nostalga, and who doesn't like a little throwback? Also, the style fits so well with the gameplay and just the concept of the shovel knight. I love it and think they did an amazing job and making every environment unique and beautiful.
The soundtrack... well I love the old 8 bit and 16 bit soundtracks whenever I would play on the NES, and it pumped you up for what was to come, like in games such as double dragon 2. It just felt goooooooodddd. This game gets the blood pumping and jams... jammin. Also they fit the environments for each different level. ITS JUST GREAT. That is really all I gotta say about that.
I mean, even the "story" if that's what you wanna call it is cool. The ending and the constant saving of Shield Knight in dreams made enough of an impact to keep me interested and emotionally engaged in the game, which just added that one more layer that it needed as a creative and interesting game.
And Replayability. Its short and sweet. It doesn't drag on, like most platformers do. Game like mario and megaman are known for their replayability and good design... most of the time. Shovel knight has that same aspect as a platformer that make it a fun game to come back to whenever you feel like it and still have a grand ole time.
10/10, definitely ranked as one of my favorite games of all time, and I highly reccommend it to anyone contemplating on getting it.

MAKE SURE YOU PLAY THE ADVANCED SERIES INSTEAD OF STORY MODE
Summary of my spoiler-free review of Story Mode:
- EXCELLENT map design
- Good puzzles but some have obvious flaws
- Good music, but not on it's own
- Okay writing (sometimes great, sometimes forced)
- Decent voice acting
I recommend this game to everyone who enjoyed Portal 2 - the shortcommings are nit-picks and won't detract from the experience too much. Additionally, many of my complaints are fixed in the advanced series.
Play as Mel as you explore old aperture before being cryosleep'd into a time period between Portal 1 and 2. The map design is outsatnding, there is eyecandy and subtle humor everywhere and a lot of areas to look at and explore, all throughout the game. The quality of the maps are on par with Portal 2 if not better, making this feel like it could have been a true Portal 1.5. However, some of the other aspects aren't on par - some of the puzzle designs have some obvious exploits that let you skip massive parts of the puzzle easily, and other puzzles have testing elements that I found completely unneccesary, as if they were red herrings (intended to not be used) which doesn't make much sense. The difficulty of the puzzles is on par with Portal 2, maybe slightly harder, which was a little dissappointing to me, HOWEVER most of the puzzles were very enjoyable because they were fizzler puzzles. For those that don't know, fizzler puzzles are very enjoyable (at least for me). One of the new testing elements is a fizzler that also kills you, so it's like a laser wall that doesn't alow objects through...in other words, it's a piece of glass that can be turned off, which already exists in Portal 2 (that jump suit you're wearing looks stupid). Something cool though is the use of water to put out fires, though it feels like a gimmick. The music isn't as energetic as Portal 2, it's actually more along the lines of Portal 1 as it is eerie and mysterious while also being very robotic. I wouldn't listen to it outside the context of this game but it felt appropriate and is well made. Finally, the dialog/writing - some of the jokes are very funny, but most of the time it feels like they are trying to repeat existing jokes from Portal 2, mostly the ones that became memes. It felt forced and it wasn't done very well in my opinion. Also unusual is that a character at first says GLaDOS's name, but then every time later they say "HER" instead. It feels weird, as if the character I was with was suddenly swapped out with Wheatley. There's even a copy of the neurotoxin hacking scene from Portal 2, except that instead of thinking with portals, you just press a button. As for voice acting, the Cave Johnson actor didn't feel very natural to me - not because it didn't sound like Cave Johnson, but because of the meme repitition I mentioned earlier. It felt like I was listening to a remix of Cave Johnson quotes. The other characters in the game are done well, though, and I felt like they were really there. If you liked Portal 2, then you should definitely play this game as you will enjoy it too. My criticisms are nit-picks and despite them the game is still great and it's clear a lot of effort went into every aspect.

In a way I'm conflicted: I thoroughly enjoyed Resident Evils 1-4, even though the first zombie in the original Resident Evil gave me nightmares at the age of roughly 8. You can say I have a hate/hate relationship with Resident Evil in general, however overcoming and defeating the game and the monsters within always came with a measure of satisfaction.
We've move pretty fast in a short amount of time: going from the glorious blocky-ness of older RE games to even refurbishing and re-releasing them as of the time of writing this review (I can't wait to see RE2 and 3 come out remastered) however we've gone away from being a Survival-Horror game with a bit of inventory management and we've moved to full blown, over-the-top Action-Shooter territory.
No longer are you hampered by a scarcity of resources, you can readily re-play stages to horde gold and ammo for your next foray into the story itself. While Resident Evil 4 struck a balance, Resident Evil 5 did away with it quite quickly. Whether this is good or bad really depends on how you approach the game, and how quickly you realize that you should take away that pistol from your AI partner who isn't quite good at it. Give her a Sub Machine Gun, you know you just spray and pray, she'll actually save you ammunition.
The most horrifying aspects of the game remain the surprise boss fights against things that will murder you quickly, but with checkpoints and "save areas" in between, you can die, re-kit, and then succeed. It is worth noting that restarting later stages is crucial, as you will often need to change your load out to face a boss or a particular situation.
The graphics look nice, but then I never put too much weight on graphics, being the kind of person who thoroughly enjoys playing games like Arcanum and Fallout, and the controls handle well with a 360 Controller, though it still bothers me that the laser reticule doesn't "shine" on walls and only on things you can "hit'.

Here's how your Arma experience is going to go. First you will buy the game and play the campaign for about an hour until you realize that its total♥♥♥♥♥♥and then move to multiplayer. You'll check out King of the Hill, Wasteland, and some roleplay servers, and rack up a hundred hours doing that. But the bread and butter of this game is the community mods and missions. I would say that 70% of the time I've put in this game has either been playing singleplayer missions with a nearly game breaking amount of mods loaded, or playing multiplayer missions with a small group of friends with that same game breaking amount of mods. Arma is basicaly unplayable after discovering the joys of mods, and that is what has kept this game alive for so long. Don't think of this game as a finished product, think of it as a platform in which you can transform it into anything you want. Want to cruise around a tropical island in a sports car with your buddies, theres mods for that. Want to cruise at high altitude raining down freedom at Iraqi's, theres a mod for that. Want in depth, serious roleplay, theres a mod for that (and countless servers). Want a basic FPS, well, you probably don't need a mod, just play King of the Hill. Want to have a hardcore military simulation or play with uber realism, you guessed it, theres a mod for that. With the help of mods (which is insanely easy since you download them right off the Steam Workshop, and the launcher is the most useful thing they've added in the game) you can turn this poorly optimized, half flushed out, game into anything, and I do mean anything. This game hasn't gotten old, and I think my hours can testify to that. I'll play this game until Arma 4 comes out, and probably even longer since all of my mods will take a while to get ported over.

Let me preface this by saying that I don't write reviews often. I'm pretty sure I've never written a review for any game on Steam ever. I simply don't see any point in putting my two cents in where others have already tred. However, this game is the exception.

So having access to something so intuitive that I could translate the action I'd use for a casting spoon into an in-game action, and get the same results is like a breath of fresh air.
There are some rough areas, specifically in audio and video while landing a large fish, but this is easily overlooked due to the solid game mechanics and familiar behaviors of the AI. The game fish behave exactly as I have experienced actual fish behaving, so the attention to detail is excellent.
If you need a break from FPS, MMO or MOBA toxicity, grab a rod and reel, throw out a line, and shoot the breeze with your fellow anglers. You'll be glad you did.

It says I played this game for three hours, but it feels like many many more as it  is one of the most tedious games I played recently. Imagine narrow corridors disguised as alleys, narrow corridors disguised as hallways, narrow corridors disguised as sewers, narrow corridors disguised as pathways between containers and you get the idea.  Eventually we will get to narrow corridors disguised as narrow corridors.
At heart most games are basically linear in concept, but this one is so obviously confined to just one narrow path that it's sucks the fun out of the game and what is more, there is virtual no story, no atmosphere , no interesting characters and no interesting dialogue to keep you going.
The gameplay itself contributes to this monotonous tedium. You spent half the time scavenging for ammo which you find in small portions but need in large amounts because all the adversaries take multiple hits in the head alone.. shooting other area's of the body just make them blink or fall down for a moment, if you are lucky. And the game throws lots of them at you.
Combat itself is an awkward affair. Nothing seems to work quite right. It is almost comical how the ai works.. with enemies lumbering towards you and staring past you while making threatening movements away from you. Combat is sluggish.
Personally I couldn't fathom why you would want to play this game when there are some many better ones out there.
If you like a game with a good story, captivating atmosphere and interesting characters, try Resident Evil Revelations 2.
If, on the other hand, you like shooters, look elsewhere as well. Give Spec Ops: The Line a try.  The combat is a lot better.
If you like a tedious monotonous linear game that you only play because you are a RE fan and you  are charmed by the hot side kick Sheva then buy RE 5.  But only when it's on sale.. for paying more than a few bucks for being bored is a waste of your money and your life.
Anyway.. if you still want to give RE 5 a try I hope you have fun.

TL;DR: Great game, not for hardcore fans of horror series, an action packed bro-op third person shooter, stupid ai controlled partner, cheesy action movie style story, presentation of game is great, gameplay elements in the game really shine. 7.5/10 Enjoyable experience.
Things to note before reading review: I've bought Gold Edition and this was my first ever resident evil game I've played.
This game is exactly as other people say an action face paced third person shooter. Its like a cheesy action movie with scripted explosions, quick time events, and even a car chase. A bro-op action shooter that never stops delivering the action. Did I enjoy it? Hell ya those 70 hours spent on the game were mainly messing around with randoms online and even beating the game on professional. Mercenaries is also a main focus of Resident evil bringing out and showing the fun and varying combat system.
Story: Its a cheesy action packed third person shooter following the footsteps of Chris and Sheva as they travel through Africa on a mission from the BSAA. Fighting against bioterrorism they fight local zombie like creatures and fight things that increase in size, bullet soaking power, and strength. Another virus is back to plague African villages and tribes with some randomly placed journals that tell deeper back stories on certain areas, people, and experiments. There is a lot of depth to the environment that resident evil 5 has laid out but its over shadowed by all those action sequences and over saturation of actions packed missions.
Gameplay: Suberb, Resident evil 5 really takes the cake as a co-op shooter. The only real problem I find in it is the quick time events that are absolutely annoying. You have a inventory system holding 9 possible objects of ammo, weapons, herbs, etc. You can find treasure to sell and use for money to upgrade weapons, buy new ones, and so much more. Shooting also has interesting aspects of being able to shoot enemies in the face, arm, or feet which will trigger 3 different types of melee attacks that you can choose. The depth and ability to perform combos is very interesting especially with a human controlled partner. This game play element is especially useful for mercenaries for comboing and extending time.
They also removed GFWL and added steamworks. I never really knew the problem with GFWL that everybody finds.
In conclusion, a great game in the aspect of game play. Capcom has really done it with this game Hardcore Resident Evil fans that wish the series would go back to its Horror roots will definitely be disappointed with this game. The story doesn't shine with anything interesting or new just overviewing another virus and some predictable plot points. Game play is great through the upgrade system, treasures, and melee attacks. Great to play with friends.

If you enjoyed playing Portal or Portal2 any one bit then you should probably give this a go.
It's free so you have no reason not to try it.
Voice acting:
Anyone that enjoyed Portal and Portal2 knows damn well that part of what made them great the dialog. Considering that there are no profits being made on the game, I had low expectations on the voice acting. It isn't horrific, but still a wee bit off. Overall decent though.
The game play difficulty:
For me, the game was challenging and made me think about what I needed to do to solve the puzzles, but not difficult to the point where I got stuck for an extended period of time in one location. I would rank it on near on par with Portal2.
Map and level design:
Considering the developers resources, I was impressed. There appears to have been a great deal of thought put into the map design. Again, the game is not perfect and you might notice flaws in a few places. Aesthetically speaking, some of the larger office buildings and rooms did not sit right with me, most notably at the beginning of the game before you get in your sleep tube. The offices aside, the vast majority of the game was remarkable, beautiful, and fit the style of Portal2 extreamly well.
Story:
Without giving anything away, I will only say that I enjoyed the story of this game. It was very well thought out, smooth, and nested itself nicely between Portal and Portal2.
Conclusion:
To be honest, it is not as polished as the retail portal games but still extreamly impressive. Just play the damn game! If you liked Portal and Portal2 you will more than likely enjoy this also. If you are confused about what I meant by the developers resources, you will understand exactly what I’m talking about when you see the end credits.

Personally, this game can pretty much be summed up in one word, meh.
This is my first SR game so unlike many others, I don't have much issue with the story starting with the killing of an iconic character [whom I have no emotional attachment], if anything, it's weird that the game at places keeps referencing this Gat person whom I'm supposed to love. This means simultenously, I have no issue with the supposed butchering of Shaundi's character, I have no inkling of her character development prior to this.
That being said, this installment does pretty much nothing to the development of its supposed main characters. The story is nothing exciting but tends to focus way too much on side characters or villians. The ending [the one with saving Shaundi & Viola] is ridiculous, even for SR's standards. There is simply so many plot-holes. Also not a fan of how the game chokes missions that are supposed to be activities down your throat if you're to advance the story. Speaking of the activities, while some are okay, a handful of them are simply a source of frustration due to the clunky AI.
Now with the DLC's. Trouble with Clones is pretty cute, but it's unfortunate that the powers usable within this DLC are not unlocked for the main game [although with the knowledge of SR4, one could see the reason why]. Genkibowl is dismissable, it's simply the main game's activities with a fresh coat of paint [sans the Sad Panda activities, but since there's only 2 of those, it doesn't add much to the DLC]. Gangsta in Space is so-so, it adds quite a few new vehicles and weapons but they are not much unique from stuff already available. The story is not bad but seriously short.
I'm also playing with the mod, Things to do in Steelport. So my review might be skewed in that sense. In any case, SR3 is again, meh. But since it's quite short, it's recommendable if only to while the time away with some silly fun.

This game took a while for me to warm up too. I loved Resident Evil 2 and 3 growing up but I didn't play any RE titles beyond those. So when I got a copy of this game I was expecting zombies and dark corridors. Instead, upon firing RE5 up I got a lot of open areas, a lot of sunlight, and infected living humans that weren't really interested in eating me. I knew that RE4 had changed things but I didn't know how much. From that first impression I didn't like this game at all. After I got over being mad at RE5 for what it wasn't, I realized that it's actually really cool. I wouldn't mind revisiting straight horror and claustrophobia but action/horror is pretty good too. So Pros and Cons:
Pros:
+Solid Controls: I favor using a XBox 360 Controller with this title and it works great.
+Plenty to do: 50 hours in and I'm not bored yet and I still haven't actually cracked into the Gold Edition material.
+Good Combat: With an abundance of weapons (w/ unlockable infinite ammo) and melee attacks this game provides for versatile play styles.
+Mercenary Mode: Practicing your combat skills never gets old for me, plus it's a quicker way to unlock extras.
Cons:
+Unlockables: After all the time I spent unlocking infinite ammo and upgrading weapons I can't use any of them in Lost in Nightmares, Desperate Escape, Mercenaries, or Versus.
+Trading Weapons: Once you have a weapon it's yours. I can't trade with friends.
+Quick Time Events: You may feel differently but I seriously hate them. There aren't a lot in this game but I wish there were none.
+No Local Split Screen: While it doesn't come up a lot, now and then I find myself wanting to play co-op with a none PC gaming friend. This game can support that with mods, I don't understand why it doesn't just support that out of the box.
Overall:
This game has its flaws but mostly I really enjoy it. I've played it through on the XBox and on the PC and it's been great.

A highly enjoyable game that is a huge step forward from its 2008 predecessor. The game is so many steps forward from Saints Row 2; but misses certain things that the previous part had.
The game can be quite challenging at times, but never to the point where it was infuriating or extremely difficult. The graphics are so many steps forward from Saints Row 2, however, the layout in Saints Row 4 is more slick and is easier to navigate through.
Steelport is a rather un-alive city. It feels like a generic sandbox city without all the good things Stilwater had. When you drove around a neighbourhood infested with gangs you really felt you were in such a neighbourhood in Stilwater. In Steelport all you really have is suburbs and suburbs with factories around them. Boring.
The soundtrack is fine. All other sounds are good.
The game controls are standard and feel comfortable. There is also the option for custom mapping.
Saints Row 3 mainly takes steps backwards in the story compared to Saints Row 2. SR2 had more believable and realistic characters and gangs. SR3 really takes this to the next level by turning a dangerous gang into a commercial brand. Dangerous gangs are no more; I haven't felt threatened by the Deckers, Morningstar, or Luchadores. And honestly,  why and when did we go from realistic gangs to Mexican wrestlers?
The characters are fun. I enjoyed the dialogue between everyone, and newly introduced characters Oleg, Kinzie, and Viola deWynter are fun and refreshing. Pierce is a significantly more fun and enjoyable character since last part. Shaundi got a complete overhaul, turning her into a more cold-hearted character.
I have all the DLC apart from the Bloodsucker Pack and the Unlockables Pack. While I wouldn't pay any more money for the DLCs separately, having extra outfits, weapons, vehicles, and missions was nice. The missions weren't too enjoyable, but they added to the gametime I guess.
Speaking abuot the game time; clocking in at a mediocre ~21 hours was disappointing. I wish I could've got more content out of this game because I felt like it had more potential.
Nevertheless, the game is highly enjoyable and if you are able to pick this game up for 5 dollars around the Christmas sale I would highly recommend it!

I deleted all of my previous writings. All you need to know is that this is not a hard-core fishing simulator. Not even close. A lot can be improved, but it seems it won't be. I'm saying this based on 30+ years real life angling experience and 1500 fish caught in this game.
Also note that you need to be a gamer (i.e. and addict) to progress in it. If' you're a normal human being with life, you will probably be irritated by extremely steep progression. It is to be changed, however, still not clear how.
However, it looks pretty and is very addictive. There ARE moments when the illusion is indeed very strong. But they get less frequent and further appart as you play more.
Ok, think of it this way.. This game is as ultimate fishing simulator, as latest Call of Duty is the ultimate warfare simulator or Dirt3 - ultimate rally racing simulator. These games may seem that to many, but if you were in the real war or raced real rally cars.... You get the point. Plus, we know that there are much more realistic warfare or rally simulators, so it can be done. With fishing situation is different. This game is quite probably the most realistic at the moment (not counting (very) old ones). But being most realistic doesn't guarantee that one is realistic at all.
And judging by all we know at the moment, the game will remain this way. There will be a lot of new content, but the fishing framework will hardly change. Hope I'm wrong.

Objectively, the reviews below saying "not recommended" are correct. The game is really not finished, and given it has an development for many years, and has not seen an update in a while, and the developer statement that he is "burned out", I would not expect any more updates.
With that said, I still spent an enjoyable month or so playing this game. Coming from Dwarf Fortress and wanting something a little prettier, this game provides a nice twist on the genre, rather than mining you "dig too deep" by hiring heroes who explore dungeons.
It provides an interesting and detailed tech tree, one of the best workshop designs I have seen in any such game (you place zones for workshops and then crafting stations within zones).
That said, I am obsessed with this genre and desperate for other games in it. If you want to try something like this but with active development and far more polished, I highly recommend Gnomoria (and keeping an eye on Stonehearth and Clockwork Empires).
I would still recommend this game, although given it is unlikely to see any updates I would personally want to see the price knocked down a little given its incomplete state.
I really hope the new developer breathes new life into this game, but I feel like once the game gets into a negative feedback cycle developers have little incentive to do so -- when everyone is panning your game on Steam and no updates have been released for a year and a half, what is your incentive to continue working on it?
Even if you decide not to buy, I would keep an eye on this game just in case things change.This game has a tremendous amount of potential, and is farther long than many games in the genre.

Rainbow Six: Siege teaches us one thing very quickly: Nowhere is safe. My only hope---our only hope---is coordination. Even then, the best laid plans of mice and terrorists often go awry.
Players have also been experiencing quite a few bugs, from little graphical glitches to more serious problems. One time my keyboard just wouldn't work anymore, but only for Siege. Other games were working just fine. I could hide but I couldn't run. Bugs and graphics aside, this is a tight, strategic shooter with great maps, destructible environments, and fast, fun matches. The core is PvP, but co-op is also available in the players-vs-bots mode Terrorist Hunt. That's a fun objective-based mode you can play with teammates or as a "lone wolf."
The smooth blend of stealth tactics and furious firefights keeps players on their toes, with the various operators offering unique ways to experience each map and game-mode. Different options for Attackers and Defenders helps keep Siege's playability levels high, and I personally can't wait to see what plans Ubisoft has for this game in the future.
I bought the game only. No dlc. I do not regret a thing. It takes a bit of grinding to unlock the year 2 characters, but it saves money. There are a few things that I would love to see change in the game.
Spawn peeking is frustrating.
Peekers advantage is annoying.
Combine both of them and it is horrible.
Glaz's buff is overkill. He was strong enough as he was.
Fuze's projectiles bounce too far, and they do too much damage.
Castle and IQ are basically useless in mid level games, beginners don't know how to deal with them and pros know how to use them.
Bartlett U Terrorist Hunt Bomb Defusal with the yellow gas is near impossible. Rainbow Six Siege is a solid FPS. The community is better than most and the developers listen to feedback, which is sorely needed and a breath of fresh air in the PC gaming world.
Of course there are some balancing, network latency, and team system problems, but Siege still has a framework that works and is constantly being improved upon. Every map has complexity that can be learned through experience, but is frustrating for beginners. Even the game system itself has so many mechanics to learn that it can be very frustrating at the start. This also gives the game great variety and replay value, however, and still retains its value well beyond a year after release. Just embrace that Siege isn't quite like the other shooter games that you play.
Terrorist Hunt lacks the variety and spontaneity that multiplayer offers, but still acts as a healthy diversion from the sometimes frustrating multiplayer experience.
Remembering how far this game has come since its beta just strengthens my resolve that it will continue to be a great FPS with a healthy population for (hopefully) a long time.
Matchmaking is broken, you can start the search, wait 4 mins then restart the search and get instantly in game.
Overall though it is a solid game with a decent community. I have experienced less cancer and less toxicity from the r6 community than the TF2 or CSGO. I would recommend the game, but buy ONLY the game first to see if you enjoy it, otherwise it is a waste of money.

Im not saying that snaking people was a very healthy mechanic when you could do that, but bring something new that makes the game fun to learn again. Adding so that fire exstinguishers could be blown up is a cool mechanic but lets be real, its used like once every 10th game. Jumpshooting was a relatively fun mechanic, I would love to see that back in the game.

The first half (roughly 5 to 6 Hours) is pretty nice, not really any horror but on higher difficulty (i played on survival) you get that survival feeling, e.g. scarce ammunition/healing items and enemys do a lot of damage.
That was pretty much the good part.
Capcom decided to ramp up the action and enemy count over the course of the game and it gets worse and worse.
The pacing is awful, there are barely atmospheric downtime sections, they throw wave after wave of enemys at you ALL.THE.TIME.  I just wished for it to be over after some time. They completely drop the ball when introducing zombies with guns which are still surprisingly accurate and do tons of damage.
And all this while keeping the tank controls from RE 4 and an annoying inventory system which is much worse this time around because the game continues in real time while you're in it.
A lot of levelparts and (boss)fights also overstay their welcome and this game would have benefited from some streamlining, content wise. The whole finale just goes on and on and on.
And don't think of playing this with the AI. Sheva is good at saving your butt when you are dying but the amount of failures i got because of her  not moving when she should, not hitting enemys but shooting half her mag in the air or standing in my line of sight.
The game turns from decently fun to a real chore halfway trough, not recommended.
Play RE4 or the HD Remaster from the first game instead.

ONLY GET THIS GAME IF YOU LIKE DYING AND A CHALLENGE.
It is not that bad of a game. If you give it enough time. If you are wanting to build an elaborate fortess with 5 stories and everything perfectly place in it, you will get mad and quite the game. Instead look at it as a survival game mod with ever increasing sieges that force you to explore the depths of dungeons so you can equip your villagers with good enough weapons to survive the 200 spiders that spone inside your base.
It does have many bugs to it: having to set flags at every square to explore a dungeon, a villager ignoring your minimum level setting and going into the 5 floor just to pickup a set of bones, the over bulky food production (only efficient way is to eat T1 food that only fills 20%), the "heroes" that drag dungeon monsters into your city, the glitchy animal farming, the complete lack of certain resources on maps (excluding that random unreachable piece of coal placed floating ontop of the lake).
But these are all part of the random events and part of the challenge. Every time you get killed off, you learn a new aspect of the game. The reason they don't explain much of the tutorial is becuase they want to you figure it out in the game.
It has a lot more depth into the game: dealing with traders, forming an army to defend sieges, creating a badger areana, wood working, smithing, fishing, glass blowing, vanities (cosmetics), inlisting heroes, killing monsters (orcs, goblins, ogers, giant, trolls, ect), a death cycle for villagers (disease, disposal of corpses/ wraiths), farming, pastry making, complex item system, and a lot more that you have to discover.
But you do not see these with just playing for the first 5-10 hours and calling it crap.

P.S.

So I'm writing this review with very little game time ON STEAM, most of my hours rest on xbox a while back but am writing a review now since I've just bought the game so am able to.
Resident evil 5 is an action game developed by capcom and released in 2009 and very much sticks to less of a horror feel and embraces its' action side.
The game is clearly MORE intended to be played with a friend as the A.I. can genuinely be terrible, if playing solo it isn't the WORST A.I. around, but there definitely will be times where it costs you a herb, first aid spray or even a death but that being said, the co-op in this game really IS fun, that's where alot of the games appeal comes into it for me, it's genuinely enjoyable.
Now Resident evil 5 is NOT the best game around, it does lack alot and later in the game really begins to feel slow and repetitive, but past that the games definitely something worth trying atleast once for the experience. Voice acting is, as always, not great, and has led me to even the point of laughter on various occasions, but that's quite honestly something I've just come to expect of capcom at this point.
Gameplay wise the game is perfectly fine, it has the resi-standard stop to shoot mechanic which can lead to some surprises when getting railed from behind by an angry man with a pipe, and feels pretty fluent down to the inventory which is very easy to use, by the end of the game there is a huge variety of guns, then upgradable with the money you get from selling various treasures found when playing through, and with some upgraded guns leading to the unlock of OTHER guns, the game is definitely not short of reasons to replay, from BSAA emblems to mercenaries mode or (like myself) just wanting the satisfaction of having every gun in the game fully upgraded, resident evil 5 leaves you with SO much to do even beyond your first completion unlike many other games where once complete, they just lack replayability.
TL:DR- Resident evil 5 is a very fun game best played with a friend but not at all unplayable solo. It holds a ton of replay value and even including the slow feeling of the late game, the quite honestly hilarious voice acting (not a good thing) and the dodgy A.I. I'd definitely say this game is worth a try! :)
Hope this review came in handy, I'm not the most experience review writer around what with this being like my 2nd one, but criticism is always accepted!

Has a bad rep for being more combat-shooter than previous RE games.
There is clear focus on the third person shooting, stagger into mele-combo punish, a couple of turret sections and fairly strict level linearity, but at least the "tank controls" were replaced by something functional, the visuals fit well with the franchise and the hub inventory system made collecting different (upgradeable) weapons an interesting side-hobby for me as I played.
If you can handle the action/co-op style focus then the usual resident evil plot sillyness is there and I personally found the chaptering of the game to be well done, it allowed for an unusually consistent plot pace and provided some replay value to more interesting areas (or to collect hidden items/farm some upgrade funds).

The gameplay has a few annoyances, such as Shovel Knight's annoying jump arc. It seems fine up until you get to a point where you have to dodge♥♥♥♥♥♥in the air while jumping across instadeath pits, and then you'll throw your controller through the monitor. You'll get hit, put in a damage taken animation where you have no control over yourself until you hit the ground, but you don't because you fall into a pit and die and lose money. Also some enemies are just way too damn fast for your slow melee attack. Since you can't move and attack at the same time fluidly I've just found that spamming the fireball kills things the easiest, which is a dissapointment.
Overall I give this game a 4 out of 5. If you have the patience for learning attack patterns its worth getting.

So I played this game for probably more hours in a couple of months than a couple of games I have owned for a year or two and I can tell you that alot of this time was fun. Until you get to the grind. If you are looking for a fishing simulator I would honestly wait for maybe a year and see where this game is in that time. Fishing isnt about catching and I dont believe the devs and many people actually realise this, its about the thrill of catching the fish, the fight and the thought that you have the chance to not catch anything or catch a fish that you can put in your personal records or the local newspaper. I am level 17 in this game right now and have caught hundreds of fish, If I was on a trawler boat sure I would accept that number but once you are grinding from what I have gathered 313 fish to get 25000 xp for level 18 to get to a new lake and actually catch some decent fish is rediculous, the process of getting this 25000 xp is pretty grueling requiring you to constantly fish the same old bass in the same old spot at the same old time with the same old lure with no real skill involved (promised dynamic fishing system not implemented). So the only way to get this XP is through "Farming" call it what you want this is not fishing its catching, when it gets to the point you are catching a fish every cast every day on the same lure it is catching, after a while this is no longer fun. When discussing this I have had the typical "well go fish somewhere else" "stop calling it farming and you will eventually stop thinking it is a grind". I am sorry but since I spent nearly a month in each of these spots "farming" it is boring and also ineficient as the lower level places give you less XP as you expect. Sure its a fishing game but not a simulation game like advertised which is sad to me. I thought the game would be fun and exciting after the new fish fights, It didnt. The only I see to really fix this game is to remove this XP system completely let people fish again, let them have fun, not every game needs to be about one upping people of stats, let people fish a spot and try to catch the biggest fish to drive a competition, lower the frequency of catches and the game becomes a fishing SIM the way it should be. Keep the money system and add more premium currencey tackle for revenue but please for the love of god dont turn this in to what everyone is comparing to a fishing MMO where it is no longer fishing. Even a license system like the hunter would do me but everyone knows that that would never work because funding a f2p game is a bad thing as as soon as money becomes involved it is p2p (Sarcasm)...

+ Replayability (Singleplayer AND multiplayer)
+ Realisic difficulty / immersion /  pick your gear / teamwork is essential (- if you're not into group games)
+ Many game modes: Capture the Island, Warfare, Exile, Life series ... and yes, DayZ.
+ "Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ did I actually crash land safely?"
+/- Serious fun. This is not meant for casual FPS players. No you cannot 360 no scope. Yes it can take hours to play through a mission and yes you can get killed only ten minutes in. That's what the restart feature is for. Multiplayer? ... Well I hope you like spectating. It can actually be fun too!
- "Realistic difficulty" / Expect to die / Here's to 30 minutes watching everyone else die / Damn AI sniped me through a tree.
- "I got Arma'd" / Those stairs/walls/1ft fall, basically the physics engine can be a monkey's paw in tight quarters
- FPS bug for high end NVIDIA cards / this is not a 64 bit game (wtf?)
- AI (An EI (enemy infantry) that turns 180 around and one shots you under a bush isn't rare.) / Other general stupidity.
While fun, this is not the type of game that you can jump into in any form of the word:
1. This game has a learning curve. The controls are just the first part and I advise you to get them set up to your needs/desires BEFORE playing seriously. Check the terrain (height vs. under ridge advantages), is there cover you can use, depending on difficulty if the AI sees you you're done for but that's AI and its cheats. These are only some.
2. This game takes more thought than you would think. Would it be best to walk around the town to your objective or directly through? The Map in topographic mode is your friend, learn how to read it and use it to your advantage.
3. Patience is key. I can't count the times I got gunned down by deciding to run without checking when I could have survived by walking through instead.
4. Missions, as stated, can take a while and I don't know of any multiplayer server where the mode allows you to jump quickly into it unless it allows for HALO jumping. Even then, have fun walking.
5. Depending on the server, playing with a group is best and using teamwork can up your chances of succeeding.
Overall, you can play this by yourself but that relies on mods or the rare gamemode (likely modded). This isn't a casual oriented game. If you're okay taking the time to learn the ropes and like your game to be a bit more serious than most with the difficulties that entails, I HIGHLY recommend this game.

Well, it's been months since any word on this game.  It's sad, but safe, to say it's discontinued.  What started as a promising but crude 'dwarf fortress with graphics', a functional prototype was quickly hashed out.  Obviously far from finished, an 'early alpha' at best, the game was near-unplayable due to constant crashes, game-crippling bugs, the most cumbersome resource management system in history, and an exponentially growing supply chain that cripples and ends every game on a sour note.  The lack of content and clearly thrown-together mechanics left everything to be desired.  And those sorely hoping for more were disappointed, as little to nothing changed over the many months since it saw the light of day.  By this point, it's a lost cause-  it can no longer hope to add anything new or compete with the myriad competition.  It will forever be known as a half-hearted attempt to alpha-scam the sandbox genre during it's boom.

This game reminds me of the old school days of Megaman, Castlevania, and Metroid (exploration, slight rpg elements, knock backs when hit).  Make no mistake, this is definitely a tough game, and it has some moments where you feel like it's just being hard for the sake of being hard.  There are some moments of pure frustration (like when you have a boss down to one or two hp's and they knock you into a pit - I actually never recall a game with as many bosses that have instant death areas; either pits or spikes).  Despite the unfair-ish difficulty at times, the challenge level overall is nice - it's just those few moments.  The checkpoints and ulimited life system may neuter the difficulty a bit, but having you lose some of your cold hard cash when you die balances it out pretty well.  Graphically, it has a very nice HD retro look, with cool characters and enemies.  The towns are lively with a few side-quests sprinkled in for good measure.  The game controls beautifully and has that "when you die it's your fault" feel to it - if you fall in a pit or hit the spikes, it's not because the game didn't do what you wanted it to.  Overall, I had a lot of fun with Shovel Knight, and for anyone who is a fan of old-school games that whip you into shape, you should definitely check it out.

4). Hit reg is still a extremely inconsistent, and all of you saying its fine are delusional because otherwise Daybreak wouldnt be talking about in what ways they are trying to fix it.
5). The shotgun is in the game at all. The spread is so much rng its crazy. When two players from the same distance hit each other once with shotgun, one has two-hit lammy and the other one doesnt even have armor, yet the guy with a lammy dies, something is obviously wrong. When getting someone down to onehit and pushing them, you are still in a bad situation because the other player can kill you in one shot and he has peek advantage so hes obviously going to shoot first. You shouldnt be punished for having better aim/positioning. Remove the shotgun and bring an SMG to the game, far less rng based.
6). There are too many cars. Its truly turned into car1z1 after the release of Z2. More carspawns, ATV spawns everywhere. And the way of fixing it isnt to buff the magnum (which is already op) or to blow all cars up after second safezone, that would ruin the game and within a month all slayers would just stop playing the game. Just spawn less cars. Copstation PV has 3 carspawns, turn it down to 2. G7 has 7 vechilespawns, turn that down to about 5. Reduce carspawns in "hotspots" where there already are a ton of spawns.
7). Hipfire is still overpowered as hell, which reduces the skillgap massively. Players with 2 hours in the game can two tap the best player in the world if theyre lucky.
8). Arclegger claimed that there are no bad spawns anymore. I can agree that if youre playing to win with less than 10 kills, sure spawns are amazing. However there new map has basically no hotspots anymore. G7, strip north of PV and the compound west of that are the only possible hotspots there are. On Z1, there were several hotspots, which were all easier to get to due ot the map being way smaller which also meant that the space between hotspots was way smaller. Warehouses, AK alley, big and small res, dam and suicide cabins. Even Cranberry could be pretty lit at times. Now you can honk your horn for 1 minute and not a single player will peek you in the city.
9). PV, and all other cities are too big. PV is suppose to be the place where you can get 10 kills without problem. Some games you even struggle to find 5 after the first gas starts spreading. The city is so big that there are no consistent hotspots. This makes the earlygame very frustrating and also boring in a lot of matches. Lets be honest, the huge park in the middle of PV is ♥♥♥♥ing useless.
10). Fighting mechanics are reducing the skillgap and extremely repetitive. Strafing one way while firing your gun, maybe crouching a bit aswell. There are no ways of outplaying opponents other than outaiming them (something which makes hit reg incosistensy even worse) Its all just really boring after doing the same thing for several thousand times. Bring back seatswapping and pronespamming, but nerf them, dont remove them. Bring in more fighting mechanics that you can use. Im not saying that snaking people was a very healthy mechanic when you could do that, but bring something new that makes the game fun to learn again. Adding so that fire exstinguishers could be blown up is a cool mechanic but lets be real, its used like once every 10th game. Jumpshooting was a relatively fun mechanic, I would love to see that back in the game.
11). The cross on your crosshairwhen standing close to a structure. Has anyone ever said that this is a good feature? Im pretty sure its all complains about this, how its completely unnecessary and shoulderpeeking is impossible if youre also prefiring.
12). Are nades ever going to be fixed? They have been like this for 4 months now and I dont recall Daybreak even metioning this a single time in patch notes or producers letter. They take so long time to throw, and if you throw ♥♥♥♥ing air instead of what your hand is holding, thats annoying. This cant be hard to solve can it?
13). The scoring system is unfair. EU spawns with 185-200 people per, while NA spawns with around 150. I know why Daybreak did this and I think its a pretty good idea to solve the queue times, but it gives EU a higher chance of getting high kill games and slightly higher scores. Im not a technician or something but doesnt more servers equal lower queue times? This can hardly be a problem considering the amount of money the game makes from all the crate they release (instead of fixing bugs). I get that crates make more money than fixing bugs etc, but keeping your players happy should imo be the highest priority.

There's more to the ugly business of war than shooting people.
Real war is about communication, cooperation, patience and logistics. There are very few games that show how real military organizations handle objectives, and honestly, Arma 3 is the best way of giving atleast a glimpse of how a real military operation may be broken down and solved.
I've got to say though,
Not at all. This game does absolutely give you a more realistic view of what real firefights are like, I.E "You can't see anything and nothing makes sense", but it is not a sim overall.
Getting arma'd is a common phrase for the otherwise great VR engine (Mostly Havok actually) ruining any house of cards you try and set up. The AI isn't too great either, and normally needs a person to keep them on a leash to get the best out of them.
But like most truly amazing games, the true magic is what you
do with it. Mods. It's a platform. Like an M16A4, it comes into it's own when you stick stuff on the picatinny rails.
If you can think of any major military commitment in the last 100 years, you can probably recreate it in this game.
Everything from WW2 dogfights, navy SEALs in 'Nam black ops, firefights in the hamlets of Serbia, cold war submarine stuff, right up to full on flag waving desert storm and street fights in fallujah.
After watching a war documentary, you can probably find the exact gun and tank someone talked about in it right down to weird sub-versions, then run around doing war like stuff with them. The community for that stuff is remarkable.
And you really can go from far above the clouds to the bottom of the sea seamlessly, on detailed maps that often extend many kilometres in each direction. Tanks, cars, trucks, MRAPs, IFVs, APCs, fighter jets, transport planes, submarines, boats, all fully functional and often lovingly detailed. If you like equipment, this is perfect if you're ok with modding.
Same is true for infantry gear. If you like a good gun, how does a few hundred sound?
Performance is infamously poor, but it's perhaps not surprising considering the sheer complexity of it all. Quality of life updates from Bohemia do come out, and it's surprising how different the game feels since release,
Buying this game does give you access to an insane amount of content and games-within-games (zombie stuff too!), but for the actual game right out of the box, it's still pretty good, especially with the Apex expansion which is wonderful.
Online community is especially good too, with even a few real serving military people. It's all very mature but friendly.
If you're even mildly interested in the military, this is a truly great game. It's not as intimidating as it sounds.

Shovel Knight is everything I wanted in a retro-styled game. Everything about it is well designed and well implemented. I suppose Mega Man meets Ducktales is my best description; Shovel Knight can jump, slash, and do a "pogo" jump on the heads of his enemies.
The game has pretty tight controls despite the retro look, and Shovel Knight is a flexible character that, despite getting lots of abilities through relics, doesn't need them. The game takes a Dark Souls approach to punishing the player for death, spurting out some money each time you die. That money can be picked up again if the player manages not to die before doing so.
The game isn't very hard, but there is a little bit of a learning curve with shovel mastery. In a way, the game lets you make the game harder by allowing you to destroy checkpoints for cash, forcing you to restart at the beginning of the level if you break them all.
Bosses are rather varied, especially considering the sort of game it is. Enemies are, too, as are the environments and obstacles. Shovel Knight can get a few upgrades to his weapon, and a few different armors with different effects. On top of this, he gets 8 "relics" that are optional (they don't come from bosses). Health and mana pools can be expanded and there are chalices that act as "sub" or "e" tanks, except that they are only filled from two particular NPCs and they have three different effects depending on the contents: full HP/MP, treasure magnet and invulnerability for 10 seconds.
I wasn't expecting the story to really be much, but it's silly, light hearted and not all that bad.
It's around the length of a Mega Man game or Ducktales for a 100% playthrough without a guide, which is about 8 hours, but the game can be completed in a speed run in well under 1:30 or so (there's even an achievement for it). There's a NG+ that makes the game more difficult, and there's a lot of Kickstarter stretch goal content that's not in yet but will be added as free updates later.
This game doesn't need a pricecut if you're at all fond of the NES era, and it's well worth the $15 bucks even without the extra content in yet.

"Portal Stories: Mel" is a fantastic little mod that puts you back in the underground labs of Aperture Science as a test subject named Mel. Featuring all of the standard Portal gameplay, the puzzles in this mod are challenging right from the start and stay that way throughout. Testing elements from Portal 2 are frequently used in new ways, along with puzzle designs that are unique from the inspiration. While the graphics aren't cutting edge, it's still very nice to look at, with the detailing and polish of test chambers and rooms in between on the level of Valve's titles. It also comes with a high-quality original soundtrack fitting each moment of the action.
In addition to the great level design, Portal Stories does an excellent job of recreating the atmosphere of the official games, delivering an interesting new story with similar tongue-in-cheek humour and vivid characterization to the source material, while avoiding the impression of being a copycat. The mod does a great job taking the player through the various parts of Aperture's extensive facility, and never dragging on too long before throwing something new for the player to tackle. Until you get stuck, that is, and even if you do there's an official walk-through you can consult if it gets really bad. If the puzzles are consistently too hard, then there's a Story Mode with simplified solutions for those who still want to experience the game without constantly finding themselves unable to progress.
All-in-all, "Protal Stories: Mel" is certainly worth playing if you're a fan of thinking games and a little bit of story. If you already enjoy the Portal series it's a must-play!

Honestly I can't think of any fishing game I have ever played that was better.   First of all the game is absolutely beautiful, the environments are very natural and serene. The water dynamics like ripples and splashes in the water are amazing. Also there are many locations and over 34 types of fish with more of both to be added in the future.
The fishing is very realistic, sometimes you can almost subconsciously feel your mouse tremble as you see a nibble and set the hook. The fight of the fish is very satisfing especially with big ones, where battles can last over five minutes.
Fishing Planet is a very relaxing type of game that you can lose hours playing. It's one of those games that you don't have to be constantly at the keyboard. You can sit back and relax while playing or get up and walk around to strech your legs, go get a snack, yet your still in the game.
The game works on a level based system where you earn XP points by catching fish. As you increase yor XP, your level rises. Higher levels allow you access to better rods, reels, baits, lures and tackle in general. Higher levels also allow you access to the other locations where the fish get a lot bigger thus the need for better gear.
The best kind of free to play model, you don't have to pay for anything. You can purchase three things with real money; in-game cash, a premium account which gives you increased xp for catching fish and DLC packs. None of these are required to play the game however. You have complete access to everything in the game for free, with the exeption of having to grind a little to earn the higher tier locations and equipment.
This game is in early-access which means it is basically an alpha. Which also means it is not completely finished and has aspects of gameplay not yet added like boats, free roaming and multi-player. These features will be added in the near future but the lack of them still does not undermine the playability of the game. Even without these features the game is still wonderful to play. It also has bugs and game mechanics that will be rebalanced as well. This is the nature of all early-access games. I played a few early-access games and this one is in much better shape than your average early-access game, try it for yourself.

In closing, Fishing Planet is completely free to play, is a small download about 2gigs and runs well on even lousy computers. Highly addictive and also very satisfying as well, what do you have to lose? Fishing Planet is an absolutely a must own game if you are any fan of fishing.

This is my second favourite RE game, after Resident Evil 4.  The gameplay is similar although I prefer RE4's inventory system - it is more simplified in RE5, also the game does not pause when you bring it up to switch items which can lead to frustration during hectic gameplay.
Graphically the game is excellent and it still looks very good even for 2015 imo.  It also runs very smoothly and is a high quality port.  Music and voice acting are also excellent.
The main campaign is a lot shorter than RE4's, my fastest playthrough was 3hrs 9mins (on a successive playthrough with upgraded weapons etc.).  If you play normally and don't rush it might take you about twice that long.  There is plenty of incentive to play through the campaign multiple times, to get all the Steam achievements, find all the treasure, buy and upgrade all the weapons and get enough points to unlock all the bonus unlockable items, figurines, additional characters etc.
The game has a great atmosphere, the action is very satisfying and the characters are likeable and you enjoy their company.  On the negative side, your partner's AI is poor at times and they often get themselves killed (because they don't defend themselves for example), don't heal you quickly enough so you die, or walk in front of you while you are trying to shoot.  On the higher difficulty levels this can be infuriating.  I have completed the game on Professional difficulty which was EXTREMELY frustrating at times - but it can be done.
The DLC is short but good fun (especially Lost in Nightmares) as is the additional Mercenaries mode with new characters.
Now that the game has Steam cloud support and has ditched the hated GFWL I highly recommend it.

I looooove this game! It brings back fond memories of my NES/SNES childhood. It isn't purely relying on nostalgia though. It is also a pretty good game - an amazingly well-made platformer. Tight controls, clever level design, interesting enemies, useful items and a gorgeous soundtrack - all of this blends together perfectly and results in a game that is a lot of fun to play. Unlike several other recent retro platformers that were inspired by some of the most frustrating and infamous NES titles, Shovel Knight isn't all that hard. Sure, the second half of the game is still challenging, but as long as you are at least somewhat competent with 2D platformers, you will make constant progress. While it isn't that hard to finish, Shovel Knight provides other challenges beyond simply completing the story. There are lots of hidden secrets that you can hunt down, there is a harder new game+ mode and you can also attempt speedruns or no-death-runs. This game has a lot to offer.
If you liked Mega Man, DuckTales and/or Castlevania, you will love Shovel Knight. If you never played any of those games, chances are you will love Shovel Knight anyway. It is one of the most enjoyable platformers out there.

This deserves deeper analysis that I'm about to give it, but this is one of my favorite "small game" experiences as of late.  When describing Towns to people, I decided it was like telling 10 people how to play minecraft… but without the patterned crafting.  So much of minecraft is lived in telling someone where to put something in a 3x3 grid, but in towns you just say "Go make a wooden sword" and they must goto the wiki on their own and look it up.
Towns places you in the traditional omniscient 3rd person viewing angle that Christ himself enjoys.   You get a randomly generated world with 11 citizens of your "Town".  You drop orders for what to do, and the citizens go do it.  Chop down all these trees I've moused over.  Harvest this apple tree.  Build this wall.  Dig this tunnel.  Oh crap, there's spiders in that tunnel.  No, no don't die… run away… crap.
And then you start a new game and realize there's much more you need to do before you plumb the depths of your little block world.
Towns is an impressively deep game where it does not appear to be on the surface.  I mean that literally as well as figuratively as while at the surface of the game it's about Townsperson happiness management (oh yea, they need to be happy, not over worked and if you can manage that, you'll get more people showing up in town… that's an important mechanic that I didn't think of until now… see… deep) and setting up replenishable resources so everyone doesn't starve and you've got plenty of wood for that epic barbarian castle you just dreamt up.  Dig down only a couple layers and there's combat to be had.  Not super impressive combat, just your people wiggling at the beast until one of them makes this strange death noise.  You can't control the combat at all.  Soldiers can be designated, even set on patrol routes, but they intervene somewhat rarely which makes taking them off labor to just stand around with the best sword you've made so far a little useless.
Again, this game goes so much deeper than I'm giving it credit for in this review… suffice to say, it's quite enjoyable. If you like economy heavy RTS, dwarf-likes or civilization games give it a whirl.  I recommend buy-in at $10, but that's only because it's a little bit of a gamble as to wether you'll like it.  I'd be willing to give this game $25, but that's knowing how much I enjoy it after playing it for hours.

This is an excellent mod and I heartily recommend playing it. The quality and attention to detail in this game is brilliant. It has a full story which fits perfectly in-between the original games. It is well voice acted. It is full of new locations with lots of little hidden bits and pieces to find.
However before playing this I read some of the other reviews which gave the impression that this was effectively a fan made Portal 3 and it is most certainly not that. The reason the game does not feel like that is firstly that it does nothing particularly new, there are no new mechanics and the story is predictable, retreading the same ground as before. But more importantly the design of the puzzles are obviously not done by Valve. Throughout the portal games they guide you through how to solve the puzzles but without making it obvious so that you feel clever when you solve them. Here many of the puzzles are much more difficult so you don't get that same sense of satisfaction of solving the puzzle you just get frustrated, eventually muddle through and feel like an idiot. If you have play a lot of the more difficult community maps then this game is likely to be much more appealing.
One other minor thing that disappointed me was you get to see Aperture in its heyday but it is not as glorious as the ruins in Portal 2 suggested. I expected it to be a bustling community full of people constantly working to push back the frontiers of knowledge with science but you are presented with an almost deserted town square.
