-------------------------
Short Review:  If you like a challenge from a charming game that resembles something out of Megaman 2...get this game.
-------------------------
Long Review:
Gameplay - - -
Shovel Knight plays much like a hybrid of Megaman 2; Duck Tales; Super Mario 3; Shantae; and Dark Souls.  If you're unaware of what these games are...it means this game is a mixture of everything great about platforming.  Each level is designed to be difficult to get through, yet not so difficult that it's impossible.  Trial and error is a big part of this game, and you'll want to invest in the various items that'll help getting past that "one spot" all the easier.
Everything in this game is balanced out so that it's fair, but challenging.  My only personal gripe with this game consists of a big sin within these types of games; "Knockback Damage."  This type of damage happens when you're attacked or otherwised damaged, and your character is forced backwards a short distance as a result.  Often times a death can occur from merely a single knockback which slings your character into a death pit.  It's understood that this is suppose to add an extra challenge and encourages planning (for gameplay improvement), however in reality it's unnecessary and quite unfair.  Platformers need to get rid of knockback damage.
Other than that, the gameplay is perfect.  The controls respond properly; the controller layout is both efficient and ergonomic; and each area is difficult enough to challenge any player, yet not totally impossible.
Music - - -
The music is your typical 8bit retro appeal.  What's important is each song is made unique, and is also tolerable enough so as not to become annoying.  Definitely great music for what it is.
Replayability - - -
Once you've beaten the game, it allows you to replay the entire thing all over again starting with what you've acculmulated through your first playthrough...BUT now all of the enemies have been re-calibrated to be much more difficult.  This in essence allows two playthroughs.  A multiplayer mode of some sort would be nice, however it's not really necessary.  With the two playthroughs you'll get your money's worth.
Story - - -
The story is perfect.  It engrosses  you in an adventure that, although not terribly original (and is very predictable), lives up to compel you to keep playing, and to actually care about these characters!  Few if any 8bit games have achieved this kind of smart and endearing entertainment.  The ending (no spoilers here) will affirm your admiration for this incredible game, and the efforts they put into the story and smart humorous dialogue.
Overall- - - - - - -
Shovel Knight proves to be one of the greatest, most entertaining games to come out as of late.  It both entertains and challenges while never making you feel like you're beating a dead horse to win.  Knockback Damage can enrage you on occasion, however with proper planning and patience many of these obsticles can be overcome.  Casual and pro gamers alike will enjoy this near masterpiece.
9/10 rating.....you and your friends NEED to get this game!
Helpful Tip:
On the very final boss, you'll be given a movable platform to which you can bounce on, to then reach the head of the final boss.  Instead of bouncing once on this platform, do a double bounce so that you'll be propelled higher than usual.  In doing this, you'll reach the head of the boss more easily, which'll make your life MUCH easier. ;-)

[NB: I played this game on PS3 with multiple completions.]
SR:TT is an amazing game IF you didn't play Saints Row 2. So while I could go on about how SR2 is superior in pretty much every way other than graphics (arguably, though), I'm going to say this: it is very fun on a sale (£2.74) and for that price, you cannot go wrong. Undoubtedly people compare this to Grand Theft Auto all the time, and as a "GTA clone" it does its job wonderfully. Music is pretty good, support for PC mods are great (and oh, this game can be something else when you use mods). I unfortunately thought the city looked quite unmemorable and meh at best (doesn't come anywhere close to many open world "GTA clones" today such as Sleeping Dogs, Watch Dogs, and the prior Saints Row titles). The game is sometimes badly written and is overdone with humour, which is unfortunate to say the least. Most of the jokes are just about sex, and they aren't very amusing. Saints Row 2 is absolutely perfect in comparison to SR:TT. However, SR2 on PC has a very maliciously bad port, one of the worst of all time. [About SR2: Firstly, for me the AI would be flatout broken, I set the difficulty on hardcore and they still couldn't hit from 10cm distance.]
This game had some rampageously poor AI at times too, but it wasn't gamebreaking or anything. Anyway I did have fun, but I would recommend Saints Row IV over this one as that one has much better comedy, missions, characters and overall script/writing. Saints Row 2 is the definite main go-to as it embodies things so perfectly in my opinion, but instead of risking the PC port, just get it on Xbox 360 or PS3.

You can basically get the max amount of health really early on in the game (after ~4 stages) and that makes you IMMORTAL against normal enemies. Having too much HP also transforms fun boss fights into button smashing karate. You basically just smash the boss as fast as you can ignoring boss attacks completely... Is that fun? CERTAINLY NOT.
Even the insane max hp is enough to make the game too easy but when you add your mana and immortality items into the mix the math goes somehow like this:
30-60s immortality from MP item usage
~3s each time you lose 1/2 HP orb (10 orbs max)
= total of ~2 minutes of immortality
We also have 2 consumables which can be easily refilled after each stage and you can decide when to use them because check points are everywhere and death penalty is a joke. Those consumables refill your HP and MP to max. So.. with them that makes:
~2 minutes of immortality * 3
= 6 minutes of immortality!!!
That's enough time to complete multiple rooms or beat the boss.
Do you still think that the game provides any challenge? Nope. If you were looking for challenge you should buy some other game.
NG+ makes the game bit harder by punishing us for 1 whole orb for each hit BUT you are dead bored of the game after completing it on normal mode and NG+ is only available after beating the game in normal mode once or by cheating. Who wants to cheat to get more challenge from games? Exactly! No one!
I also have to mention spikes and pits which kill you instantly but spikes can be avoided with immortality item so let's not count those. We are left just with pits for challenge... so how many challenging pit areas we have in the game? In my opinion only the last few rooms of airship and final boss IN THE ENTIRE GAME.
I recommend this game to anyone looking for casual platforming game. The story sucks so hopefully platforming is good enough for you. For anyone else: wait for -75% price or buy another game.

ArmA is not so much a military shooter as it is a military sim. Ultimately you will of course find that the devs decided to ignore realism in favor of gameplay, but mostly it is the best you'll get on the market.
What will you get with ArmA3?
A gigantic map, aproximately 225 km^2 of somewhat diverse realistic terrain including but not limited to multiple towns, settlements, A salt lake, hills, mountains, monasteries, beaches etc. Not included in those 225 km^2 is the underwater terrain which you can explore and play in. There are coral reefs, boats, submarines etc.
Realistically behaving weapons that feel nice. The sounds may not be perfect but they work. You can choose between firemodes, zeroing, magazines, attachments... A benefit from the big map also means that your Sniper can actually be used for long distances for once. Personally I sniped from around 2km range and there is potential for more extreme ranges for sure.
Destruction. All Houses and buildings are destructible.
Vehicles that feel like a own simulator including a big amount of Helicopters, Jets, Cars, Tanks, Artillery and Anti Air. There are both civilian and military vehicles.
A very deep control system meaning that every stance you can ask for will be possible to archieve.
The best and biggest community for milsim and realistic gameplay where playing tactical actually matters.
A lot of different ways to play (the following are not the names but how they play like) : "second life" aka civilian roleplay, Coop milsim, Deathmatch, DayZ without zombies, Attack&defend, Last man standing, Battle royale, Capture points, hold a town.
A extensive modding community which creates a lot of content.
Nice developers that listen to the community and actually seem to care for it.
When investing in the DLCs you get carts (it's pretty much a joke at this points. It is literally just carts and some carting clothing), more helicopters, more cars, more weapons and the best game map I have ever seen. Equally big as the first one but with dense vegitation, ruins, modern cities and generally a very different feel than the other map.
What you will not get:
A easy to learn game. You will die. A lot. The controls feel far too detailed until you actually learn them. Gunplay for snipers, movement, driving etc want to be learned.
There will be Bugs. It got better but they are still there from time to time. You may glitch from times to times (it was some time when it last happened to me but it is still there).
It will destroy your pc at times. Good rigs will still have problems having very good framerate. Accept that it doesnt run that well , it doesnt for everyone else either. Framerate and performance is more reliant on processor speed than it is with normal games. Your performance is also incredibly dependant on the server you are on.
There is elitism at times. Most people I ever met were incredibly supportive. They were nice and tried to get me to learn. Accept though that noone will want to fly with you when you are new to flying. You will most likely crash or land so bad that they die before even touching the ground. Occasionally though you meet the guy who will♥♥♥♥♥♥you for not being fast enough at grasping the situation etc.
The reason why I love this game and recommend it to everyone though is something you need to experience for yourself. There are Moments that you do not get from other games. I spent 20 minutes in a house, under heavy fire trying to survive while my team drove from 4 Cities away with a car to extract me. In every other game you'd just respawn. Here people actually help you out.
I pushed with a group of 7 players that all talked on the radio (as in called out enemy movement etc) from house to house while a helicopter in the sky rained shells on enemy positions at night and illuminated the night with the gunfire.
I sniped with some complete strangers that spottet enemies for me and told me ranges. I did the same for them. We still play together at times.
I wasted incredibly much time on collecting and transporting wares to buy weapons later to rob other players in "Life".
I sniped and got sniped. I shot players and got shot. I laughed and lied. Ultimately my best gaming moments happened in this game and still happen. I met people and learned languages.
See you on the battlefield.

SR:TT is an amazing game IF you didn't play Saints Row 2. So while I could go on about how SR2 is superior in pretty much every way other than graphics (arguably, though), I'm going to say this: it is very fun on a sale (£2.74) and for that price, you cannot go wrong. Undoubtedly people compare this to Grand Theft Auto all the time, and as a "GTA clone" it does its job wonderfully. Music is pretty good, support for PC mods are great (and oh, this game can be something else when you use mods). I unfortunately thought the city looked quite unmemorable and meh at best (doesn't come anywhere close to many open world "GTA clones" today such as Sleeping Dogs, Watch Dogs, and the prior Saints Row titles). The game is sometimes badly written and is overdone with humour, which is unfortunate to say the least. Most of the jokes are just about sex, and they aren't very amusing. Saints Row 2 is absolutely perfect in comparison to SR:TT. However, SR2 on PC has a very maliciously bad port, one of the worst of all time. [About SR2: Firstly, for me the AI would be flatout broken, I set the difficulty on hardcore and they still couldn't hit from 10cm distance.]
This game had some rampageously poor AI at times too, but it wasn't gamebreaking or anything. Anyway I did have fun, but I would recommend Saints Row IV over this one as that one has much better comedy, missions, characters and overall script/writing. Saints Row 2 is the definite main go-to as it embodies things so perfectly in my opinion, but instead of risking the PC port, just get it on Xbox 360 or PS3.

A continuity of RE4 with a few interesting added twists, is what I would call RE5. On a visual level, it is really compelling when played on high end computers. It may not come accross as the most original, as many of the enemy designs are recycled, like the chainsaw Majini, the Gatling Gun Majini, the new El Gigante, or the giant bat. What RE5 does do, however, is create new dimensions to what has already come before. The QT events are a little more elaborate, and, I would say, a little more demanding than before. The tricks, traps and instant death situations are certainly more startling and when you fail them, the results are quite spectacular.
The extra melee moves refine the gameplay. The extra punches and kicks from various angles introduce a wider range of tactics to use against the enemies, making the combat system more realistic and fun.
RE5 is best described as a refined version of RE4. If the predecesor had been made with this kind of graphics and enhanced gameplay system, the successor would have been even greater. As it stands, RE5 is a compelling adventure and a fitting end to Las Plagas. They go down, but not without a fight.
In terms of level design, RE5 has some fine settings, both in terms of atmosphere and ambiance. The arid climate of Africa is well implemented, even though the blurred vision effect was not implemented. The set pieces of the boss fights are certainly well crafted.
This game is for the fans and newbies alike. It has qualities to please both groups and hook them on the series. The only drawback is that RE5 does not shine for its originality.

I'm a big fan of the Saints Row series. I haven't played 4 but I love 1-3, and I plan on playing 4 soon. If you're debating on whether to get the base game or the Full Package, you're not missing out on a whole lot with the DLC, but the extra 5 bucks does get you quite a lot of new items and some new missions, and it's worth it for the missions more than anything else.
Saints Row is the one series that really competes with Grand Theft Auto in a lot of players minds. The first game took that formula of open world criminality coupled with a tongue-in-cheek mentality to a new level and added in a great deal of variety on the sorts of activities you could do in-game. But in my opinion the first game still took the gangland setting and story a little too seriously. Saints Row 2 was essentially the same game as the first with more activities and content, but pushed the boundaries of seriousness with the storyline a little farther. Saints Row 3 is the pinnacle of that progression. It continues the same themes and storyline but now absolutely everything is over the top and ridiculous, and I love it.
I've heard it said that some people don't like that about Saints Row 3 but in my mind this is the world I've always wanted Saints Row to inhabit. Crime and ultraviolence in cartoonish proportions and absolute ridiculous♥♥♥♥♥♥happening on a regular basis.
Just to give you an example, one missions I did involved a chase through the streets in carts pulled by BDSM gimps in leather masks, and another mission involves you signing onto a Japanese game show that involves gunning down furries.
I do have some problems with the game but none of them are a big deal. The clothing system, even three games in, still doesn't make sense to me. It allows for a huge amount of customization but you have to buy each clothing piece 100 times if you want 100 different color variations of it.
As far as customization goes, Saints Row is one of the best series, bar none, but even though it was pretty simplistic, Saints Row 2 had some options to customize your safe houses, which this game doesn't, and this game doesn't allow you to purchase strongholds in areas either, although I guess the tradeoff for that is that I spent all my money on upgrades anyway.
For most missions you're not allowed to use vehicles stored in your garage which is disappointing but understandable since I have attack helicopters and fighter jets stored in there.
Also, even though Saints Row is really good about actually rewarding you for all the stuff you do in-game, most of the rewards for challenges are just small cash payouts, which is disappointing.
Overall though I'd definitely recommend Saints Row 3 to just about everyone who likes games. It's been said before but this is a series that isn't ashamed to be, and is perfectly aimed at, being no more or less than just a lot of fun.

Beautifully crafted level design that make the player think before he leaps. The artwork is fantastic.... unique and eye popping color palletes for each level that are a rare treat for the eyes. Shovel Knight makes the player crave to continue inbetween playtime.
The adventure is so grand, fun, adorable, and yet treacherous at the same time. The hidden mini games and challenge levels are not just thrown in there like most platformers with an overworld map, but integrated nicely into the game. Much like that of which Super Mario Bros 3 had. It visits and pays homage to the truly great platformers that shaped our love of the genre. Games like Megaman, Castlevania, Mario Bros, and Duck Tales have all their best qualites meshed into this game.
Look.... the title screen is even amazing. The way the shovel is your cursor. The epic title music. Hell, even the the selecting sound when you choose your title screen option is awesome and satisfying as hell.
We're missing so much of that in most games today. Using stock sounds and cheap looking menus because so much time and money is pumped into rendering the next best 3D characters and worlds. Now theres nothing wrong with that, and I'm certainly just as impressed as anyone to see just how far we can push our graphics card limits and get lost in these hyper-realistic environments. BUT Shovel Knight proves that even today game designers can still dish out 2D games that rival the enjoyment and playability of any next gen console games.
This game is a must have for any fan of platformers, retro console games, good music, or having fun.
I highly reccomend you buy this game and play it til the end. After that look up the cheats and have a blast.
Shovel Knight is a masterpiece and anyone who doesn't own this game is missing out on an unforgettable experience and piece of gaming history.
Kudos to you Yacht Club Games. I absolutely cannot wait for your next game. :)

A continuity of RE4 with a few interesting added twists, is what I would call RE5. On a visual level, it is really compelling when played on high end computers. It may not come accross as the most original, as many of the enemy designs are recycled, like the chainsaw Majini, the Gatling Gun Majini, the new El Gigante, or the giant bat. What RE5 does do, however, is create new dimensions to what has already come before. The QT events are a little more elaborate, and, I would say, a little more demanding than before. The tricks, traps and instant death situations are certainly more startling and when you fail them, the results are quite spectacular.
The extra melee moves refine the gameplay. The extra punches and kicks from various angles introduce a wider range of tactics to use against the enemies, making the combat system more realistic and fun.
RE5 is best described as a refined version of RE4. If the predecesor had been made with this kind of graphics and enhanced gameplay system, the successor would have been even greater. As it stands, RE5 is a compelling adventure and a fitting end to Las Plagas. They go down, but not without a fight.
In terms of level design, RE5 has some fine settings, both in terms of atmosphere and ambiance. The arid climate of Africa is well implemented, even though the blurred vision effect was not implemented. The set pieces of the boss fights are certainly well crafted.
This game is for the fans and newbies alike. It has qualities to please both groups and hook them on the series. The only drawback is that RE5 does not shine for its originality.

This is probably the best fps i've every played, and yes that includes overwatch. At a glance, it might not seem to have any value beyond a pub game or be p2p, but this isn't true. Competitive is pretty good outside of the in-game mode, and items can be exchanged 1:1 at scrap.tf, most 'essential' unlocks can be given through achievements, and the stock weapons are the midpoint of balance between unlocks, meaning that they're almost always the best due to their reliability and power. If you haven't given this game a chance, then try it, if you have given it a chance, try and look at it again
PROS
- This game has the best relation between combat, movement strategy and satisfaction that I've ever played in an FPS.
- The classes are really well designed and defined, as well as the combat and strategies between them.
- If you invest time into it, rocket jumping and all of its offshoots, i.e. sticky jumping, beggar's jumping, detonator jumping, medic surfing and so on, and how to take these into advanced levels or integrate them into gameplay is some of the most satisfying/engaging♥♥♥♥♥♥that i've ever encountered in a game
- Every time you die it's pretty much your own fault, and you can always learn and grow in the game, i've hit 2600 hours at this review and i've only moderately mastered all of the classes, this game has so much depth it's mad
- There's a really wide variety in maps, modes, and strategies
- It's a bit reductive to say that tf2 has 9 classes - almost every soldier primary and secondary recontextualises his strengths and weaknesses, and some unlocks, such as the demoman's shield, create an entirely different class. With the medic, all of the medi-guns are very unique and strategies around uber and how to counter your opponents uber are all interesting, just to give a few examples. Spy, pyro, engineer and sniper all have interesting diversity as well
- Overall nutty gameplay and depth if you're willing to put in the time or learn
CONS
- The game's bloated, too many hats that ruin class recognition and tf2's excellent original art design, too many useless weapons that confuse new players, too many aids/cheesy mechanics/weapons that can't be removed due to not being able to fairly compensate players, or just left to be ignored by nerfing to hell, e.g. crit-a-cola
- Competitve mode exists entirely outside of the game, don't be fooled into thinking that tf2 isn't competitive, it's just that the competitve mode (at the time of this review) is completely redundant and♥♥♥♥♥♥ google tf2 center or competitive tf2
- There's also a really large dissonance between casual and competitive, there's no casual 6s mode
- It's really hard for new players to pick up, the tutorial is very incomplete and mechanics/many classes need a significant understanding to use against good players
- It's really hard to pub-push in some situations, unless you have a very good player on your team, due to the spammability of defence classes like heavy and engineer on last points, which is a core issue
- A lot of default settings are really poorly optimised/optimal for players to the point of retardation on install, I have no idea why this hasn't ever been addressed by the tf team
- Dev team is kind of inactive (and consists of 6 programmers), but not really, there are some really old bugs that haven't been fixed, like when you change from a class with a shotgun to engineer, your shotgun disguise is the primary weapon of the other class - this has been around before the game was f2p. However, the team manages to provide good updates/content when they need to, or maintain the game on a broad level.

Plants vs Zombies is an old game that still holds it's own. The setting is your house where you are in charge of planting mutant plants to defend your home from zombies. You meet only one other character called Crazy Dave, 'cause his shop is, "Crazy!" This tower defense game will challenge your mind as you progress to more difficult levels. What Pop Cap Games had created is a game that is one of the most addictive of it's kind.
You won't grow tired with Plants vs Zombies as there is a variety of plants (towers) to use. Each plant can be used tactically, like using a Hypno-Shroom against a zombie. Just as the plants name implies it hypnotizes the zombie to fight for your side, obviously recommended for tougher enemies . There are plenty of other plants of it's ilk in this game to meet your strategic need.
Plants vs Zombies has plenty of other challenges like, mini-games, puzzles and survival modes. The mini-games range from plant zombies that shoot back at you, to playing whack-a-zombie. The puzzle mode gives you a chance to play in different modes as the zombies or a breaking a pot game. (Where is Link when you need him?) Survival mode is similar to adventure mode; it just has more challenging levels. Then, there is a Zen Garden you can unlock as you progress through adventure mode. The goal there is to make a money farm for your grinding and to help grow a talking tree. So, yes plenty of other things to do long after you have finished adventure mode.
What kind a game has so much replay value? My wife and son still enjoy playing it, years after it's release. It is a shame we won't likely be seeing a true sequel for the PC, but at least it's on your mobile phone. (Thanks EA...) Plants vs Zombies has plenty of fun for everyone of all ages. This game can stand tall for being one of the best games of it's genre and for the price. Why not pick one up for yourself?

Sadly, it adds no new mechanics but it makes the ones already in intermingle in great ways.  It's kinda like how those amazing baked goods ingredients are great alone but combined become amazing.  I'm talking of pie, of course.  Cherries, bread, and cream are great alone but combined are great, assuming the baker knows what they're doing.  And Prism Studios know what they're doing.
Since it takes place before Portal 2, but after Portal, Aperture is still a destroyed wreak - although you get to see some of it before it Chell did her thing.
You control Mel, a Olympian from the 1936 Nuremberg Olympics who didn't win silver even though she deserved too.  The companion this time around is another core named Virgil who, unlike 'some' cores, wants to be your friend...eventually.  First he tricks you but you don't really get a say because the game is linear so, you'd met him anyway.  He is somewhat inept though.  Surprised?
As you traverse the ruins of old, OLD, Aperture to get free of your orison you do typical Portal things with 70's era equipment.  Portal 2 is the highest rated game on Steam so the devs said, if it ain't broke, don't break it.  They did, however, pump up the difficulty.  This game is very hard, at least for me.  As I said early, the devs took everything great about the Portal 2 pie and made it bigger.  Also, it's made of something you can't digest.  You will get frustrated, angry mad, rage quit etc. but that makes the reward so much more worth it.  Screaming at the top of your lungs how amazing you are never felt so good if you get through a puzzle without a guide.
The game plays great with no bugs outside of the occasional achievement not clicking (or maybe I just didn't do it right, who knows. I should play it again!).
It's free, it's Portal, it's fun, you get to destroy a spider with a caterpillar’s head who keeps shooting you.  Go enjoy the Cave Johnson impersonation.  #RIPCompanionCube

I *really* loved this title.  What sets it apart from other zombie games is that you are *completely* defenseless.  Your only chances of survival are to run and hide like a scared little girl.  You will spend more than a few moments cowering in a dark corner, hoping that a scary zombie won't see you as he passes by.
Also unique to this game is the "sanity" mechanic.  As you stray too long form the light, witness paranormal events, or are confronted by zombies, your character will gradually lose his sanity.  This leads to effects such as your screen taking on a liquid appearance and odd halucinations of bugs crawling on you.  Eventually, all you will be able to do is crawl desperately away from your enemies.  Of course, your sanity can be restored by finding a safe, well- lit area.
Overall, a very unique, scary, and suspenseful game :).

If we're lucky, they will include RE5 gold content for free with this Steamworks update. Gold had Mecenaries reunion - co op mercs and it was awesome, with oldschool RE characters in it. It also has Lost in Nightmares which, compared, to RE5 is a real survival  horror game, and Desperate Escape which shows Jill's part of the game after you find her.
Despite it's downsides, it's still a decent third person shooter and a good co op game. At least it's not RE6.

The game plays relatively smoothly and seamlessly, but there are several problems with it.
First and foremost, there's the problem with the hit detection and damage counter. When you die, you often see things like "You were hit 2 times for 165 damage. You hit them 12 times for 40 damage." It doesn't take a genius to determine that that's just not feasible. Sometimes, I even "get hit 0 times for 100+ damage", proving that there is something seriously wrong with core mechanics in the combat system.
Second of all, the weapon balancing for certain weapons is absolutely broken, especially concerning the AS50 rifle and the M4 STAR 10. The AS50 not only deals 2.5 times as much damage as the maximum health of a player, it is essentially a substitute for short-range weapons like shotguns, which is highly uncharacteristic of a sniper rifle and frankly ruins the game.
Speaking of shotguns, the M4 STAR 10 semiautomatic shotgun is also extremely overpowered. Its one-shot capability and blistering rate of fire make it virtually unbeatable. Anyone who uses either of these guns frankly takes all the fun out of everyone else's experience.
The game has potential, but the inherent flaws in the combat system and overpowered weapons completely ruin the game.

This is my game of the year for 2014.
1. The 8-bit graphics
The graphics in this game have amazed me and given me a somewhat nostalgic feel of playing games on the nes. Another great thing about this is that it never makes fun of itself for being a retro looking/feeling game. (*cough cough retro city rampage * cough cough) With the constant overflow of old looking games, this one really stands out, especially for its beautiful animations.
2. The level design
The level design is also very creative, one minute throwing me into a village reminiscent of Zelda II and the next, leading me underground to fight a giant mole-monster-humanoid-thing. This game is loaded with variety, and the platforming is pixel-perfect.
3. The difficuly
No game I've ever played before has ever made me slam down on my computer's keyboard as hard as I did when I kept falling into the same pit over and over again. But it wasn't the game's fault for the "clunky platforming", but mine because I knew I had messed up. The game is unbelievably hard, but it also has such a forgiving death system that makes it very beatable, and with enough practice you can get amazing at every single level, and then go back to find all the secrets that you missed.
4. The music
The Shovel Knight soundtrack is probably one of the best soundtracks ive ever heard in a game, if not the best. The chiptune flows beautifully into your ears. It sounds like 8-bit heaven, and I would without a doubt reccomend for everyone to download the soundtrack off of the official Bandcamp page.
And I've just scratched the surface. But if you want the full deal, I would totally "dig deeper" and give this game a try, wether you like classic games or not.

This is my game of the year for 2014.
1. The 8-bit graphics
The graphics in this game have amazed me and given me a somewhat nostalgic feel of playing games on the nes. Another great thing about this is that it never makes fun of itself for being a retro looking/feeling game. (*cough cough retro city rampage * cough cough) With the constant overflow of old looking games, this one really stands out, especially for its beautiful animations.
2. The level design
The level design is also very creative, one minute throwing me into a village reminiscent of Zelda II and the next, leading me underground to fight a giant mole-monster-humanoid-thing. This game is loaded with variety, and the platforming is pixel-perfect.
3. The difficuly
No game I've ever played before has ever made me slam down on my computer's keyboard as hard as I did when I kept falling into the same pit over and over again. But it wasn't the game's fault for the "clunky platforming", but mine because I knew I had messed up. The game is unbelievably hard, but it also has such a forgiving death system that makes it very beatable, and with enough practice you can get amazing at every single level, and then go back to find all the secrets that you missed.
4. The music
The Shovel Knight soundtrack is probably one of the best soundtracks ive ever heard in a game, if not the best. The chiptune flows beautifully into your ears. It sounds like 8-bit heaven, and I would without a doubt reccomend for everyone to download the soundtrack off of the official Bandcamp page.
And I've just scratched the surface. But if you want the full deal, I would totally "dig deeper" and give this game a try, wether you like classic games or not.
TENOUTTATEN.

Definitely one of the most fun pixel-y games I've played. While it is a 2D platformer it doesn't necessarily feel like it's trying to copy the feel that games from a couple of decades ago evoked. Meaning -- it's not like a good 90% of these indie games out there that bank solely on the fact that they're "nostalgic" to draw in the player.
This game subtdly combines elements from a bunch of different older games and makes them into something completely unique. The map is similar to Mario World 3, the gameplay and fighting style is similar to Megaman. To me though, the real kicker is in the item collection, which is similar in a way to A Link to the Past. While Zelda games are specifically notorious for this (aside from the original), most games nowadays use items in a very one-dimensional way. You play a level/dungeon/etc, get the item, and use the item to beat the boss. The same can even go with armor -- get an upgrade where you get more magic, and the level will require more magic. Yet in Shovel Knight, every item you get can truly have value in nearly any level of the game. Often, an item you get early on in the game can even be more useful later in the game than it was initially. This is, in my opinion, what set Shovel Knight above many of the other pixel-y games that are out today.
All in all, Shovel Knight is a truly enjoyable experience. With great gameplay, great aesthetics, and a great soundtrack, Shovel Knight is definitely a game worth its $15. Although it isn't the longest game, there are so many nooks and crannies and secrets to discover within the levels that its easily replayable. I'd give it an 8.5/10.

If you have a friend you're looking to play a game with on the other hand, this is probably the game you're looking for. Sheva is notoriously, profoundly stupid when controlled by the game's partner AI, but when a buddy is playing with you everything just seems to work out fine. As a co-op experience, it's one of the best ones out there honestly, about half of the mechanics are centered around having a friend control the partner and they work spectacularly well. As a solo experience...pass. I seriously think the reason Sheva is so mind-numbingly stupid is because Capcom wanted you to persuade a friend into buying a second copy of the game, and now that's a series mainstay. Go figure.
I recommend buying on certain conditions; one, that you don't mind supporting the modern RE/Biohazard formula with your money vote; and two, that you have a friend who is interested in playing it. If either of those conditions aren't met, you probably won't enjoy the game all that much.

So, Saints Row. What can I say that you people don't know yet? This is the series that tried, in its two first instalments, to be Grand Theft Auto; only to be considered a clone of said franchise. When the third game came around, the devs pretty much threw out the window any hope of becoming GTA, and instead made a game that was GTA on crack. And they nailed it.
The Saints are a criminal gang that ever since the first two games have only increased in popularity with the general public, and now they have fans cosplaying as them asking for autographs at the same time they are in the middle of a bank robbery. And the Saints are happy to oblige, for now they have their own brands of merchandise and have pretty much become cultural idols. You play as the boss of the Saints, a fully customizable fill-in-the-blanks character that has just arrived to a new city, Steelport, fresh for the taking. Who is going to stop you?
Why, The Syndicate, that's who! Three gangs have banded together to overthrow you and act as the main antagonists in the game, not to talk about the police forces not being too happy to have you around, and the goverment has started to take matters into their own hands. They will everything in their power to screw you over. So it's up to you to beat the everloving crap out of them to show them who's boss around this parts.
And that's about it, this game is GTA with a ridiculous history, a bombastic cast and the most overkill arsenal you can imagine at your disposal. This game's only goal is for you to have fun. And, yes I did play Saints Row 4 before SR3, and found out why people say this one's better. That being said, I still think SR4 is good, but SR3 is definetely better.
+ Tons of stupid fun. Seriously, parting ways with the conventional GTA formula and amping everything was the best decision the devs could have made.
+ Moddable (not easily, though).
+ You can use a three-barreled-shotgun to set people in fire, and them proceed to use a Fart In A Jar (yeah, that is a thing) to stun them and then blast them into oblivion with an oversized♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or fight numerous mercenaries on a tank, while free falling from a recently destroyed plane (destroyed by you, that is), and survive the fall unscathed, but you have now, somehow, accidentaly caused a zombie apocalipse. As you can see, the Saits Row formula is not as much "Why?", as it is "Why the hell not?".
+ For some reason, it's one of those games that you want to 100%. I don't know why.
+ The story is genuenely good, while not the selling point.
+ Co-op. Everything is better with co-op.
- Despite what I said before, the combat can get a little dull if it lasts more than what it's supposed to. Especially in the later game, in which you a pretty much invincible after innumerable upgrades. The exception being having a five-star wanted level on both the police AND the gangs, when things are just to hectic for you to care how overpowered you are.
- I recommend that you never purchase the über-tier upgrades (unless you are aiming for an achievement), which litterally gives you immunity and infinite ammo, amongst other things. The game is just not fun anymore if you get them.
- The DLC. Oh, the DLC. You probably won't care if you bought the GOTY Edition, but if you didn't, prepare to be dissapointed. With the exception of the additional side missions and some cosmetics / weapons, there really isn't much in there that is worth your money.

To be honest, like almost everyone else in the world who has played this game, I loved it. It is an almost perfect masterpiece. Almost perfect.
The positives are, well. The graphics are colourful and the characters are well animated. The tiles are used perfectly to tell the player what is normal, what is breakable and what can lead to a secret area. The music is amazing. My favourites include La Danse Macabre and An Underlying Problem, but the other songs are still amazing too. The gameplay is pretty damn great. The controls are tight and jumping is quite precise. The difficulty is mostly fair and the unlockable items all have their uses (although there are a few that are much more useful than others). As for the bosses they are done in a way that once you know how to avoid each attack, they are managable.
But, I have to be a bit honest here. At points, it feels cheap. I beat the normal game in a few hours, and out of the main game, there were a few annoying levels. I found Polar Knight, Mole Knight, and the first Tower of Fate stages to be quite unfair. Not entirely, just at points. I still enjoyed playing the levels though. I do have to say the money drop on death mechanic is... wierd. Sometimes when you die (in lava or in a bottomless pit) there is no safe way of getting it back. But it wasn't day ruining.
Overall, I give Shovel Knight a 9/10. It's really fun. For anyone who likes Zelda 2, Castlevania, Megaman, Duck Tales or Super Mario 3, this is a game for your collection. It is hard, but what's wrong with a challenge? It's mostly fair, and unlike many other indie platformers, this deserves £11 of your money. It's good. Go buy it. :)

Recommendable for anyone, but in particular those who miss the colorful good old days.

This game gets a lot of hate.  Sure the game isn't completely polished and it does suffer from a bug here or there, but really there aren't as many bugs as people make this game out to have.  I play BF4 as well and I find it has just as many bugs as this game, and the reviews for BF4 aren't as 1 sided as Tactical Intervention, when they really should be, not to mention BF4's god aweful client side / server side prediction hit test system.
Tactical Intervention is a server side hit detection game, with multiple game modes.  There are TDM style matches where you respawn after a few seconds, OR there are other game modes where you do NOT respawn, and have to wait for the rest of your team to either die too, or complete the objective in time... the ladder is by far the more fun of the two types as it promotes team play.
There objective modes like, plant the bomb, rescue the hostages and protect the VIP.
Protect the VIP is one of the most fun game modes in my opinion, especially the maps where you start in vehicles and have to stop or protect the VIP depending on which team you are playing on.  You and your team pile in a couple of cars and and have a shoot out while driving, the chaos is so much fun.
This game has the worst metacritic score out all the free to play games on steam which made it stand out for me, I downloaded it because I wanted to play it and see how bad it was and laugh, but there weren't any laughs to be had.. except those of enjoyment as this game is honestly a lot more fun than a lot of alternative shooters, free or otherwise.
Some people call it pay to win, but I disagree as you can buy mostly everything with GP (an in game currency rewarded each round for actions you perform, the better you do.. the more GP you get)   You can either rent or perminately buy weapons and equipment... oh and you can get an attack dog, which is pretty neat.  One thing you cannot buy with GP are new player skins, those you have to pay real money for, but other than a visual change they do nothing.  AND you can still get new helmets, gloves, boots and belts using GP anyway, which also give a visual and stat benefit to your character.
You start of with 50,000 GP and all but 2 or 3 guns can be permantly bought for that price.  (ranges from about 18,000 to 70,000ish GP on the weapons)  it does take some time to gain GP so you may be best renting a weapon for a day for the fraction of the cost first to see if you like it, before you perminately buy it.  Buy the time you are done fully testing the weapon you will probably have made back the GP you spent on renting it anyway.
You can also interact with a lot of objects like fire extingishers, gas canisters, you can rappel down a building..  and drive cars, trucks and an airport luggage taxi.
I can't stress enough though how much you should just try the game for yourself.  The game was to be the next counter strike and made by counter strike's co creator, but I think thats where the reviews went bad.  I believe counter strike players (there are a lot of them) expected this game to be better and possibly a replacement but it didn't turn out to be their cup of tea perhaps.  I recommend this game, it gets a lot more hate than it deserves.

I haven't played such a great game in ages!
Shovel Knight brings back the fun and challenge of the old side-scrolling platforms from the 80s and 90s, but it remixes everything to create something new and fresh.
This game is flawless.
The story is simple, but does it's job, the challenge is perfect, the controls are absolutely tight and responsive, the graphics awesome and the soundtrack incredible!
The best thing is that every single level is different from the previous one.
Both graphics and type of challenges/enemies/puzzle change every time, so it's impossible to get bored!
The game is hard, (not insanely, though), but never unfair.
If you die it's only your fault, and every level can be completed with a bit of practice.
The graphics are awesome! True 8 bit style (which is quite hard to replicate in such an elegant way), but with a much richer colour palette than every NES game put togheter, and the animations are amazing.
The soundtrack is a tremendous achievement!
I haven't been listening to such a great soundtrack in ages! Lovely tunes to pump up the action and i sometimes listen to it while doing other stuff..
I'll conclude with a special mention to the boss battles; many and quite elaborated.
If you like 2D (old school) Platform/SidesScrolling games, you'll love this one!
Pros:
- Nice Channalge (Hard, but not impossible)
- Tight and precise controls
- Amazing 8-bit graphics
- Unbelievable Soundtrack
- Amazing variety (in a matter of levels and type of challenges)
- An Achievment Hunter's heaven (There are many fun challenges)
Cons:
- NOTHING (and i haven't been writing something like this in a long while)

So I made a review before, but it was more of a troll/funny review, so after playing the game for 70h and experiencing Operation Health and now Operation Blood Orchid, I decided to delete it and just make a new one.
I'll start this review up with negatives. Get those out of the way and then move on the positives.
Now don't let this discourage you. These are more of technical issues. If you are very fragile and technical bugs can♥♥♥♥♥♥you off, Siege might at this point be a bit of a tipsy option.
There are other issues outside of ping/lag/netcode that can be most of the time hilarious. If you are person who gets easily triggered by clunky netcoding - stay away for now.
Now enough craping on this game. Ubisoft on this OP Blood Orchid is working on the netcode issues and making sure that higher ping doesn't give advantage. Hopefully they fix it.
Now let's talk about...
I don't want to make this review too huge so I'll try to be as short and clear as possible.
-Operators are diverse and extremely fun.
-Gameplay is usually slower paced, but if you know what to do, you can play more fast-paced aka use rush tactics. Of course, that depends on what operator you play. Some have more movementspeed while sacraficing armor and vice-versa.
-Big variety of maps and most are balanced except a few.
-Graphics and optimization are nearly perfect. For a competitive shooter, game looks fine and it's one of the finer optimized games. So good job to Ubi in this case.
-Tactical gameplay. It's not your average shooter where you rush in with no brain and get rewarded and get kills. You can, but you need to be extremely careful and have really good map knowledge.
-Unlocking operators is done with either Renown (in-game currency you earn for playing matches) or real money using RS6 credit. Does that make it Pay2Win? No. You can unlock lots of operators just watching 3 tutorial clips and playing Situations, which is like short singleplayer missions which you can complete less than an hour, if you don't die all the time and then you can buy several operators. More expensive operators from DLC are most expensive and take little more grind than usual.
And biggest plus to the game...
Yes. Rainbow Six Siege comes with free content and free updates. Only thing you "buy" is new DLC operators which you can buy with in-game currency. Otherwise, all updates and content is free, even skins for weapons and Operators.
My specs:
GPU: AMD RX470 Nitro + OC edition (4GB)
CPU: AMD FX 4100
RAM: 8GB RAM
MOBO: ASUS M5A78-M LX3
Windows 10 64 bit.
I get 60-70 constant FPS on medium-high settings with ocassional drops to 50 when there is lots of explosions or huge shootouts, which doesn't happen a lot. All in all, if you have a RIG like mine or close to it, you can run it perfectly fine.
For me personally, the technical issues can be annoying, but they don't overwhelm the good sides of the game.
I personally rate Siege with a very solid 8/10 and would be 9, if some of the technical issues were fixed. As I said above, Ubisoft said they are working on fixing the ping and netcoding issues. New updates and expansions have been planned for long-term, so expect a constantly updated game.

On a general whole the game feels like a labor of love, small details like gems floating underwater, the various mini-bosses that travel around the map and a difficulty curve so well tuned that the entire game steadily feels more and more challenging but at no point feels unfair or boring ( I didn't even realize how much harder the levels got until I revisited some of the early levels ). The bosses in particular are worthy of note, the way that they use mechanics taught throughout their level while still feeling fresh every time you fight them is impressive to say the least. Just Greenlight perhaps, but either way I won't be buying a game until it's fully released from now on, and I wish Steam would pull this game off the store and stop putting it on sale. It's a skeleton of a game and will never be more than that.

Plants vs Zombies [Steam - PC (Popcap's website)]: 7.3/10
This strategy/puzzle game blew up pretty much as soon as it came out, and it was the first game (whether people knew it or not) whose popularity and sales was greatly affected by the Let's Play community.
In this silly game, you use various plants to fend off zombiez from getting your brainz. As you progress in Adventure mode, you unlock not only various plants that do different things, but also different modes to add some variety to gameplay.
The strategy part, for the most part anyway, is fantastic. This is the reason why the game is as popular as it is. In the beginning, everyone is going to have their own unique way of playing. Strategies will also vary depending on what kind of level you have. There's a normal day level, a night level, fog level, pool level, and roof level. All of these have varying challenges that prevent or allow certain types of plants from being used.
100%ing this game (which is what I did for the sake of this review and my future LP) means completing the adventure mode, every minigame, every puzzle, every survival level, and buying everything in the store at least once. I'll go through each of these in that order.
The adventure mode is a good introduction to the game. It slowly teaches you how the game works and how to use each plant. As far as difficulty goes, it's pretty great. It's easy enough for you to be able to never die, but challenging enough for you to be anxious about what you should do next. The different kinds of zombies have different strategies you can use to defeat them. Not only will there be zombies with greater defense and even speeds, but there will be types of zombies that do entirely different things. I must applaud this game for giving us the option to not only defend against each kind of zombie if we so choose, but also see in advance what zombies will be appearing and in what quantities. This was incredible foresight.
The minigames mode is pretty fantastic. It includes a couple dozen different kinds of minigames introducing new types of challenges. You have to clear every one of these to get all of the minigames, and there are minigames that no one likes, but overall it's a great mode.
The puzzle mode has, I believe, two different types of puzzles. Clearing these levels will give you different levels of challenge for these types, and eventually you'll earn the endless level for that type of puzzle. They're not bad, but I think the difficulty ranks up a bit too quickly in the endless.
Survival mode is self explanatory, just survive as long as you can. In survival mode, the levels will be all of the different settings twice, an easy version and hard version. Once you survive a certain amount of flags on these levels, you can unlock survival endless. This survival endless is what I was anticipating the most, but was disappointed in it, and I'll explain why later.
I must say, money doesn't come all that easy in the latter half of the game. You'll get enough money to buy all of the plants relatively easily, but good luck grinding for enough money to get the various gardens. Gardens are essentially where you grow plants to sell money. You get plants by random drops, or by buying them in the store. This is essentially a way to grind for money, but it isn't nearly fast enough, and for a while you'll be taking one step forward and two steps back because of how much money you have to throw down to even grow the plants. In all honesty, once you buy all of the various plants for battling zombies, you're good to just never buy anything ever again. For the most part you'll be getting different kinds of plants in adventure mode, but you can buy super powerful plants in the store. These plants, however, will have to be planted over and already existing plant to be put into effect. The effectiveness of these things is well worth it, though.
This is where the game sort of bites itself in the♥♥♥♥♥ unfortunately. Ironically by adding these super fun and powerful plants, the game becomes less fun. There is essentially and ultimate strategy you can and WILL use over and over again, using these super powerful plants. If there is an ultimate weapon, the player IS GOING TO USE IT. You can't use any differing strategy either, because this strategy is pretty much the only way to last in survival endless. Survival endless ranks up in difficulty way too fast, and it introduces an even tougher zombie while they're at it. Luckily, the adventure mode on your second playthrough will automatically choose random plants for each level to add some more challenge, but at this point you'll just be sick of the game.
That's why this game doesn't score AS high of a score as it could. It's not a game you can play for more than 15 hours and still enjoy. It'll get really dull after a while. Despite this, this game is a must have. I'm sure in a few years I'll be able to play this game all over again and enjoy it as I did a few weeks ago. It's one of the more definitive strategy games out there.

2 parts Mega Man & 1 part Super Mario 3; an homage to old-school 8-bit platformers. I absolutely loved this game.
Pros:
- Challenging platformer with tight controls (xbox 360 controller d-pad)
- No-fluff Zelda-style inventory menu
- A brilliant soundtrack that is collected piece-by-piece throughout the Shovel Knight universe
- Super Mario 3-like overworld; random encounters included
- Level gimmicks (in a good way), such as a wind that blows you towards danger, a dark level that is periodically lit up by lightning, and ice levels that carry your momentum more than usual
- Enemy variety and memorable bosses
- New Game plus

Cons:
- Short game; just under 5 hours on my first blind playthrough (NG+ and free DLC cures this concern)
- The bosses are a bit on the easy side.  I definitely struggled more with the levels than the boss fights
- Filling two chalices with Ichor of Renewal (full health) is a bit overpowered
- The default control for using your magic (up + attack) is not ideal.  This can lead to catastrophic deaths due to accidental usage.  Luckily, they've included the option to assign your magic to a specific button (RB for xbox 360)
- The pits.  Some pits are instant deaths while some pits allow you to advance through the level.  It's fairly intuitive due to the way the levels are designed, but it's not always obvious
- The pacing is a little off at times.  Sometimes there aren't enough enemies and too much platforming, and vice versa
- Checkpoints can be a bit unfair.  There are stretches in the game where the difficulty between checkpoints is 2 or 3 times harder than the previous stretch between checkpoints
My Cons list is a little longer, but I am being super critical of an awesome game.  The good outweighed the bad tenfold.  I enjoyed my time with Shovel Knight, and I think any person that grew up in the NES/SNES era of platformers will as well.

Before I got Shovel Knight, I knew little to nothing about it, and I was actually deciding between buying either this or Rayman Origins. A friend suggested I get this instead. I did so.
My already high expectations (as I had heard it was really good,) were blown away by just how masterfully crafted this game is.
Imagine, several fondly-remembered NES platformers (Mega-Man, SMB, Castlevania, etc.) were merged together, slowly but surely.
It is then carefully finished up as all of the awful tropes we hated in said games (sudden unexpected deaths, weird stiff controls, etc.) are picked out and thrown away.
Now imagine it being coated in original ideas, an AMAZING soundtrack (I'm a sucker for amazing music,) and a whole lot of heart from the dev team.
With this, you get Shovel Knight.
The difficulty is surely not child-level, but suprisingly not hair-tearingly frustratingly difficult. I beat around half of the bosses of this game on the first try (Including some I'm sure infuriated others possibly, (
) but not because they were too easy to me, oh no. They were damn hard, to be sure. But it was because the game is so
with its difficulty. You remember those days in NES games when you were given like, no reaction time to an enemy's attack, or a trap that instanly kills you?
Yeah, this game has NONE of that.
: It still has many places where you can instantly die here, oh yeah, but it gives you
enough time to quickly react to them all.
This game takes all the good things in old games, only the good things, and adds in a special, original flair of its own.

Before you buy, (who is looking to buy this game anymore??) be sure to check out various reviews and decide for yourself what you expect.  Yeah, there are bugs, the game is unfinished.  At launch, it was one of very few city building sims on Steam that had that element of RTS/Hero management.
Banished for the same money is a near-AAA experience, so don't go buying this game unless you own that or Cities: Skylines.  If you are into resource and development sims then Factorio is infinitely a better choice.  There are others, but I'm only naming ones I have a lot of experience with.
Towns can be considered an early Java template game, it doesn't stray far from what you usually see in typical browser games, but I love it and that's that.  This game has a much better experience than Towncraft, an abandonware game that is way worse of a consumer-trust relationship.
Make sure you educate yourself if you're actually consider spending full price on this game.  There are hundreds of games on Steam that would probably be better suited for that amount.  If you want a unique glimpse into what was one of the "founders" of how Steam became the conglomerate of early access/scam gaming, you won't be disappointed.  And hey, once you get past the bugs and logic-defying mechanics, you might even enjoy playing it a little bit.  I sure as hell did, and that was back when this game was front and center in the Steam Drama world.

This is a fun little town simulation game with challenging gameplay and lots of facets to it.  I have definitely enjoyed it, despite the fact that I have gotten stuck numerous times trying to figure out how to progress which leads me to the game's problems.  This is still in development, and it shows.  A lot of aspects aren't explained very well and a lot of things about your villagers are hard to control.  For example, to get more villagers your villagers need to be happy.  Happiness is influenced by numerous factors, how nice their rooms are, what variety of things they have to eat, what kind of decorations they have to look at but also how much work they have to do.  If they have too much work they get stressed but if they have too little they get bored, there's no way to tell villagers how much of their time to spend relaxing and how much working (aside from a somewhat unpredictable job assignment system).  There is a great community forum with a lot of mods for the game and that helps but I cant help but wish they had more streamlining.
Pros:
Neat Concept
Good Mechanics
Tons of replayability (due to procedural generation)
Fun and not overcomplicated sim
Cons:
Less-than-optimal controls
Poor in-game instructions
Just fun.

So what do you need to run this game? 1gig of ram, a 1.2Ghz processor, and 50MB of hard drive space. Perfection, proper optimization. Ok, having reviewed the game again, it still seems to me like this is a very hit or miss game.  On the one hand, it's a game with the interesting premise that you're creating a town to attract heroes to fight in the dungeons that are invariably discovered beneath the town.  On the other hand, it's bogged down by horrible micromanagement through clunky menus.
Before you find yourself running a town worthy of adventurers coming to visit, you have to BUILD the town.  You start with a handful of people standing around with their thumbs up their asses waiting for you to tell them what to do.  You tell them to grab some fruit and put it over there in a patch of ground we'll call a stockpile.  You tell them to chop down trees and put the wood over there in a different stockpile.  You designate certain areas of ground as a room for various purposes and then have to figure out what order you're required to build the furniture for these rooms.
So you want beds for your people to sleep in?  You're gonna need a carpentry bench in a carpentry zone.  What about food more filling than apples and pears?  I guess you're gonna need a baking table and a baking oven in a baking zone.  But wait; there's something about this baking oven being made out of stone.  Now you're going to need a masonry room and an appropriate table in an appropriate zone.
This kind of crap takes place all the time in this game. Oh and it's also set to some mind numbing repetitive music barely above "bad midi song" level. The characters themselves aren't very well animated and most might as well be colored stick figures.  I mean, you tell your guys to chop down a tree...do you see them pull out an axe and swing it at the trunk?  No, you see them stand next to a tree for a few minutes while a chopping sound effect is played and then you're treated to your character hauling a log across the map to a stockpile (if you bothered to make one).
This game has a lot of promise and I've actually had this game since it was "officially released" waiting for it to live up to that promise.  It hasn't done it yet.  Oh and about that official release:  It basically went from alpha to final release overnight.  Had steam's "Early Access" been a thing at the time it would have been a perfect candidate for it.  Instead they released it as if it were done when just a day before it was "alpha" quality...but again, that wasn't really an option for them and they were desperate to make sales.
Now, in the time since the game went "live" on steam to the writing of this review, they've put up a few updates and it does look like they've fixed a few things here and there, but it hasn't changed to the point where I could wholeheartedly say "yes, buy this game!"  It's still got a rough and unfinished feel to it, and if they'd take some time to polish up the UI, add some more variety to the music, and redo most of the graphics, it would at least look like they've made some progress.  Instead it's all "under the hood" stuff with very little outward change from the earliest version on Steam.
If despite all of this you're still willing to buy the game, yes, you can easily sink 10-20 hours into it (I've almost sunk 20 into it when it was in its most broken state) because you get that feeling that somehow you're slowly making progress in the game and building something.  It's not entirely unsatisfying...it's just not entirely satisfying either.  If you buy it, lower your expectations and I'm sure this game will meet those lowered expecations and maybe even surpass them.  If instead you go into it expecting a great and polished game from the start, you'll be let down hard.

I liked this game so much I played it through twice in a row, back to back.  It's like a really good Mega Man game that's also heavily inspired by Duck Tales for NES, with a Mario Bros 3 world map and some Zelda 2 style towns full of cute animal people and lots of nods to Castlevania and other NES games.  It really all fits together into the best possible NES game, having learned from everything that works.
Also there's no "game over" for dying too much.  This alone causes a huge improvement over its source material.  Instead, there's a clever risk/reward system in place where you can destroy checkpoints for money, or attempt difficult "feats" (achievements) such as collecting no gold, eating no food, taking no damage on a boss, or completing the whole game in an hour and a half.
Some non-NES games I like that this reminds me of:
- Mega Man 7 for being a graphics-upgraded NES game without the acrobatic controls of the X series, and because it features Protoman so much and lets you get his shield.  Shield Knight is kinda like Roll and Protoman mixed together.
- Mega Man ZX Advent for the emotional boss characters.
- Drilldozer for clever mechanics such as the fist and rapier you get later in the game.
